We compared intubation outcomes across trainee groups.

Results: Over the 1,404 encounters during the study period, 642 (48%) were primary intubations performed on pediatric patients by an emergency medicine, pediatric or PEM trainee. A total of 343 (53%) first attempts were by emergency medicine residents, 254 (40%) by PEM fellows, and 45 (7%) by pediatric residents. The overall trainee first-attempt success rate was 471/642 (73%). Conclusion: There was no difference in first-attempt success and adverse airway outcomes between emergency medicine residents and PEM fellows. Pediatric residents have lower first-attempt success and higher adverse airway outcomes than emergency medicine residents.

item.description:

Methods: We conducted an ambispective observational cohort study of adults undergoing VBG testing at a single urban academic emergency department, with prospective enrollment and index-data collection and retrospective ascertainment of 48-h outcomes. Conclusion: In this single-center cohort of adult ED patients undergoing VBG testing, no association was observed between peripheral venous pO2 and 48-h clinical deterioration. Adding venous pO2 did not improve apparent prognostic performance beyond age and lactate. We cannot exclude smaller associations or potential utility in selected disease-specific populations. Confirmation in larger multicenter cohorts using consecutive enrollment and external validation is needed.

item.description:
Objective: Optimal transport strategies for severe trauma remain debated, particularly in Asia. We evaluated the association between interhospital transfer and functional outcome and its consistency across Asian trauma systems.

Methods: This cohort study used the Pan-Asian Trauma Outcome Study (PATOS) registry. We analyzed patients with severe trauma (Injury Severity Score > 15) in South Korea, Malaysia, and Vietnam (2015-2022). The exposure was interhospital transfer (Transfer) versus direct transport to a definitive-care hospital (Direct). The primary outcome was a favorable functional outcome (modified Rankin Scale ≤3). The primary model was a country fixed-effect logistic regression estimating the total effect; country-specific estimates and a transport-pathway × country interaction were pre-specified.

item.title: Am J Emerg Med: Injury patterns and early operative demand in a combined military and civilian casualty cohort: A single-centre study from the first 11 weeks of the 2023 Israel-Hamas war
item.category: The American journal of emergency medicine
item.description:
Introduction: Modern asymmetric warfare and large-scale terror attacks produce distinctive wounding patterns that differ from conventional state-on-state conflict and impose specific early demands on receiving trauma systems. The 7 October 2023 attack on southern Israel and the ensuing war generated a compressed surge of combined civilian and military casualties. We characterized injury patterns and linked them to early in-hospital resource use at a single tertiary trauma centre across the opening weeks of the conflict.

Methods: We performed a retrospective descriptive cohort study of 192 consecutive trauma casualties admitted between 7 October and 24 December 2023. Demographics, mechanism of injury, injured anatomical regions, Injury Severity Score (ISS) and acute interventions were abstracted from the institutional trauma dataset. Mechanism and anatomical categories were not mutually exclusive. Variables were summarised as medians (IQR) or counts (percentages); missing data were not imputed and percentages were computed over non-missing observations.

Results: Casualties were young (median age 24 years, IQR 21-35) and predominantly male (84.4%). Penetrating (43.2%) and shrapnel (31.2%) mechanisms predominated, followed by acoustic trauma (12.0%). Extremities were most often injured (lower limb 41.7%, upper limb 35.4%); 68.8% had at least one extremity injury and 37.0% had two or more injured regions. Median ISS was 9 (IQR 4-16); 26.5% of those with a recorded ISS had ISS ≥16. Blast and crush carried the highest median ISS (25 and 16). Early resource use was substantial: 23.4% required emergency surgery via direct emergency-room-to-operating-room transfer, 10.9% mechanical ventilation and 5.2% packed red-cell transfusion.

Conclusions: This extremity-predominant, penetrating-and-shrapnel profile, with a small but disproportionately severe blast and crush subgroup and frequent acoustic trauma, translated into early demand for emergency surgery, ventilation and transfusion. These patterns support resourcing limb-salvage and damage-control surgery, blood-bank and intensive-care readiness, and audiologic follow-up in military and mass-casualty trauma planning.

item.title: Am J Emerg Med: Subcutaneous insulin for mild-to-moderate diabetic ketoacidosis: a scoping review and implementation framework
item.category: The American journal of emergency medicine
item.description:
Purpose: Diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) is a common emergency department (ED) presentation associated with high morbidity, mortality, and healthcare utilization. While intravenous (IV) insulin remains the most common treatment, emerging data suggest subcutaneous (SUBQ) insulin may be a feasible alternative for patients with mild-to-moderate DKA. This scoping review summarizes current evidence of SUBQ insulin use across a broad range of clinical and operational outcomes in DKA and provides an implementation framework for SUBQ insulin for mild-to-moderate DKA in the ED.

Methods: We conducted a scoping review of PubMed from inception through February 2026 for adult studies evaluating SUBQ insulin for DKA. Two investigators independently screened studies, with disagreements resolved by consensus. Data were charted and synthesized across clinical, operational, and implementation outcomes.

Results: A total of 117 articles were identified and 13 included. Available evidence suggests SUBQ insulin may achieve similar time to DKA resolution, compared with IV insulin in select patients with uncomplicated DKA. SUBQ insulin offers potential operational benefits, including reduced intensive care unit (ICU) utilization, shorter ED length of stay, and improved resource optimization. Patient selection criteria, dosing and monitoring strategies, and implementation approaches are summarized. Limitations in the literature include small sample sizes, single-center designs, heterogeneous protocols, and the exclusion of several higher-risk patient populations.

Conclusions: Evidence suggests SUBQ insulin pathways achieve similar clinical outcomes and may reduce ICU utilization and improve operational efficiency in select patients with mild-to-moderate DKA. Because most evidence originates from small, single-center cohorts, future studies should focus on larger, more generalizable populations.

item.title: Am J Emerg Med: Prehospital factors associated with calcium derangements upon arrival to the trauma center from scene - A subanalysis of a multicenter prospective study
item.category: The American journal of emergency medicine
item.description:
Background: Existing data suggests that hypocalcemia may be a factor in the lethal diamond of trauma. This could offer a potential opportunity for prehospital interventions to address these derangements. We performed a preplanned secondary analysis of data from a prospective multicenter study on calcium derangements in hemorrhage patients upon arrival at trauma centers.

Methods: We conducted a prospective multicenter observational study of trauma patients admitted at the highest level of activation for three participating centers where an ionized calcium level was measured upon arrival. Data from the prehospital records were collected from the Emergency Medical Services reports. We compared study variables between patients who were hypocalcemic, eucalcemic, and hypercalcemic.

Results: There were 1270 participants enrolled in our primary study, of whom 1047 arrived by EMS from the scene meeting inclusion for this analysis. Of these, 235 were hypocalcemic and 39 were hypercalcemic upon arrival. Patients with calcium derangements had lower survival compared to patients without derangements. Of those who were hypocalcemic, 32.8% received prehospital blood products, compared to 25.6% of those who were hypercalcemic upon arrival. There were 5 (12.8%) who were hypercalcemic that received prehospital calcium, potentially indicating iatrogenic hypercalcemia. Elevated prehospital shock indices were associated with both derangements. Of the 718 who received no fluids or blood, 116 (16.1%) were hypocalcemic and 27 (3.7%) were hypocalcemic with 2 hypercalcemic participants receiving calcium. Of those 136 that received a blood product prehospital, 77 were hypocalcemic (56.6%) with 1 receiving calcium, and 10 (7.4%) were hypercalcemic with 3 receiving calcium, and the remaining were eucalcemic with 4 (2.9%) receiving calcium.

Conclusions: Both hypocalcemia and hypercalcemia occurred in the setting of blood product and no blood product administration. Our study suggests that currently available assessment methods are inadequate for predicting the presence of a calcium derangement, both high and low.

item.title: Am J Emerg Med: Magnesium sulfate therapy for adult emergency department patients with acute asthma: A narrative review
item.category: The American journal of emergency medicine
item.description:
Background: Magnesium sulfate (MgSO4) has been used for decades as an adjunctive bronchodilator in acute asthma exacerbations refractory to first-line therapy, but its role in adult emergency department (ED) care remains debated.

Objective: To review the evidence for intravenous (IV) and nebulized MgSO4 as adjunctive therapy in adults presenting to the ED with acute asthma, to clarify how the pooled analyses and the largest individual trial relate to one another, and to compare this evidence with current guideline recommendations.

Methods: This is a structured narrative review. Records were identified from a PubMed search using a single search phrase (19 records), supplemented by targeted Cochrane Library and guideline-body searches performed in August 2026 (14 records) and by backward citation searching. Screening and data extraction were performed by a single reviewer. After removing duplicates and one record excluded for population mismatch, 29 records were assessed for eligibility. Ten provided extractable magnesium-specific efficacy or safety data, 5 primary randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and 5 systematic reviews or meta-analyses, which are presented separately because the reviews pool overlapping trials. The remaining 19 records were used only as background. Eighteen additional eligible RCTs included in these reviews were not identified by our search; these are listed, and their contribution is represented only through the pooled estimates of the reviews that include them.

Results: In pooled analysis, IV MgSO4 was associated with a modest reduction in hospital admission (Cochrane 2014, 11 trials including the 3 Mg trial: OR 0.75, 95% CI 0.60-0.92; number needed to treat approximately 14) and some short-term improvement in lung function. The largest individual trial (3 Mg, n = 1109), which contributes to that pooled estimate, found a similar but non-significant reduction in admission with IV MgSO4 (OR 0.73, 95% CI 0.51-1.04), no benefit from nebulized MgSO4, and more adverse events with active treatment than with placebo (15.6% vs 10.1%; OR 1.68, 95% CI 1.11-2.52), most of which were minor. A larger lung-function benefit at the lowest baseline FEV1 was supported by one trial's prespecified interaction analysis, but a larger reduction in admission in the most severely obstructed patients rests on a small subgroup and was not confirmed by a test for subgroup differences across trials. A 2023 adult-specific meta-analysis found no statistically significant pooled lung-function benefit by either route. Commonly reported adverse effects were flushing, fatigue, nausea, headache, and transient hypotension.

Conclusion: IV MgSO4 may provide a modest benefit in selected adults with severe asthma exacerbations that do not respond to initial therapy. A greater benefit in the most severely obstructed patients is plausible but has not been established. Nebulized MgSO4 has no convincing evidence of benefit in adults. Major guidelines (GINA 2026, BTS/SIGN 158 [2019], and NAEPP EPR-3 [2007]) support IV MgSO4 as a second-line adjunct for severe or life-threatening exacerbations unresponsive to initial therapy, and GINA has not recommended nebulized MgSO4 since its 2025 update. Clinicians using IV MgSO4 in severe refractory asthma should expect a modest and uncertain benefit and an excess of minor, but rarely serious, adverse events.

item.title: JAMA Netw Open: Preschool Physical Activity Policy and Children's Physical Activity: A Pragmatic Cluster Randomized Clinical Trial
item.description:
Importance: Evidence regarding the effectiveness of physical activity (PA) policies within preschool settings remains limited.

Objective: To evaluate the effectiveness of a cocreated preschool-level PA policy on children's accelerometer-measured PA during preschool hours.

Design, setting, and participants: This single-blind, parallel-group, cluster randomized clinical trial was performed at public preschools in Stockholm, Sweden. Of 156 randomly sampled preschools invited, 124 were randomized. Children aged 3 to 5 years with parental consent were recruited from September 14 to December 11, 2020, baseline measurements from September 23, 2020, to January 22, 2021, and 6-month follow-up from March 8 to June 11, 2021. Statistical analyses were performed from March 6, 2023, to October 25, 2024.

Intervention: A cocreated preschool-level PA policy implemented for 6 months vs usual practice.

Main outcomes and measures: Prespecified primary outcomes were between-group differences in change in moderate to vigorous PA, total PA, and steps during preschool hours, measured using wearable accelerometers.

Results: Among 3751 children (mean [SD] age, 4.44 [0.86] years; 1934 male [51.6%]), 1960 attended intervention preschools and 1791 attended control preschools. All 124 preschools completed follow-up; data were available for 1530 children (78.1%) in intervention schools at baseline and 1435 (73.2%) at follow-up and 1430 children (79.8%) in control schools at baseline and 1356 (75.7%) at follow-up. Intention-to-treat analyses included 3417 children (1770 intervention and 1647 control). Moderate to vigorous PA increased from 27.4 to 33.0 minutes per day in the intervention group and from 27.6 to 33.0 minutes per day in the control group (difference in change, 0.3 [95% CI, -0.7 to 1.3] minutes per day; P = .57). Total PA increased from 177.7 to 185.3 minutes per day in the intervention group and from 176.5 to 184.5 minutes per day in the control group (difference, -0.3 [95% CI, -3.3 to 2.7] minutes per day; P = .84). Steps increased from 5415 to 5953 per day in the intervention and from 5549 to 6078 per day in the control groups (difference, 8 [95% CI, -118 to 133] steps per day; P = .90). No participants withdrew because of adverse events.

Conclusions and relevance: In this cluster randomized clinical trial, a cocreated preschool PA policy did not increase children's PA beyond usual practice after 6 months. These findings highlight the complexity of translating policy adoption into measurable behavioral change and of detecting such change in preschool settings.

item.title: JAMA Netw Open: GLP-1 RA Prescribing in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes and Cancer
item.description:
Importance: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) are increasingly used to treat type 2 diabetes, yet little is known about its utilization patterns in patients with cancer history, given limited oncology-specific guidance.

Objective: To evaluate trends and factors associated with GLP-1 RA use among Medicare beneficiaries with type 2 diabetes, comparing those with and without cancer history.

Design, setting, and participants: This retrospective cohort study used Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results-Medicare linked data to identify patients diagnosed with 7 common cancers in 2010 to 2021 and preexisting type 2 diabetes before cancer diagnosis. A noncancer cohort with type 2 diabetes was identified from a 5% random sample of Medicare beneficiaries and matched 1:1 to patients with cancer based on sociodemographic characteristics; controls were assigned a pseudo-index date corresponding to their matched patient's cancer diagnosis date. Beneficiaries were followed up annually until death or December 31, 2022, for TM or December 31, 2021, for MA. Data were analyzed from December 2025 to July 2026.

Exposures: Diagnosis of 1 of 7 common cancers.

Main outcomes and measures: Any GLP-1 RA use. Proportions of beneficiaries with any GLP-1 RA use annually were stratified by traditional Medicare (TM) and Medicare Advantage (MA). Multivariable logistic regression examined (1) differences in GLP-1RA use between cancer and noncancer cohorts with and without adjusting for sociodemographic characteristics and comorbidities and diabetes-related complications; (2) cancer-specific factors associated with GLP-1RA use among the cancer cohort after 2018.

Results: A total of 373 278 Medicare beneficiaries (mean [SD] age, 76.1 [6.6] years; 188 746 [50.6%] female) with cancer and diabetes and 373 278 noncancer controls (153 358 unique beneficiaries) were included. GLP-1 RA use increased from 85 beneficiaries (0.5%) to 9083 beneficiaries (8.2%) and from 138 beneficiaries (0.9%) to 9300 beneficiaries (6.2%) in the cancer and noncancer cohorts, respectively, from 2010 to 2022 under TM; a similar increase was observed under MA. Despite higher unadjusted GLP-1 RA use among the cancer cohort than the noncancer cohort (probability difference, TM: 1.19 [95% CI, 0.94 to 1.44] percentage points [pp]; P < .001; MA: 0.45 [95% CI, 0.21 to 0.68] pp, P < .001), adjusted analysis showed no significant differences in GLP-1 RA use under TM (adjusted probability difference, 0.16 [95% CI, -0.10 to 0.41,] pp; P = .22) and lower use among cancer cohort under MA (-0.52 [95% CI, -0.76 to -0.28] pp; P < .001). Complications or comorbidities, including obesity (adjusted probability difference, TM: 3.35 [95% CI, 3.10 to 3.61] pp; P < .001; MA: 2.42 [95% CI, 2.19 to 2.64] pp; P < .001), dyslipidemia (adjusted probability difference, TM: 2.26 [95% CI, 2.03 to 2.50] pp; P < .001; MA: 1.80 [95% CI, 1.57 to 2.03] pp; P < .001), neuropathy (adjusted probability difference: TM: 3.91 [95% CI, 3.64 to 4.19] pp; P < .001; MA: 3.17 [95% CI, 2.94 to 3.41] pp; P < .001), retinopathy (adjusted probability difference, TM: 2.02 [95% CI, 1.78 to 2.27] pp; P < .001; MA: 1.84 [95% CI, 1.63 to 2.06] pp; P < .001), and chronic kidney disease (adjusted probability difference, TM: 2.01 [95% CI, 1.76 to 2.26] pp; P < .001; MA: 1.63 [95% CI, 1.40 to 1.85] pp; P < .001) were associated with greater likelihood of GLP-1RA use. Within the cancer cohort, breast (adjusted probability difference, TM: 1.05 [95% CI, 0.43 to 1.66] pp; P = .001; MA: 0.89 [95% CI, 0.37 to 1.41] pp; P = .001), gynecologic (adjusted probability difference, MA: 1.13 [95% CI, 0.45 to 1.81] pp; P = .001), and prostate (adjusted probability difference, TM: 1.30 [95% CI, 0.72 to 1.88] pp; P < .001; MA: 1.07 [95% CI, 0.56 to 1.58] pp; P < .001) cancers were associated with higher GLP-1 RA use than colorectal cancer, while pancreatic cancer was associated with lower GLP-1 RA use (adjusted probability difference, TM: -2.55 [95% CI, -3.17 to -1.93] pp; P < .001; MA: -1.64 [95% CI, -2.23 to -1.05] pp; P < .001).

Conclusions and relevance: In this retrospective study of Medicare beneficiaries with type 2 diabetes, GLP-1 RA use increased substantially and primarily was associated with metabolic risk profile, with limited associations with cancer status. item.title: JAMA Netw Open: Operational Challenges During Public Health Emergencies in Safety-Net Hospitals
item.description:
Importance: Safety-net hospitals (SNHs) serve as essential public health hubs, providing direct clinical care and critical social services to vulnerable populations, yet gaps persist in their ability to reliably deliver these essential services during disasters.

Objective: To identify common challenges faced by SNHs and actionable approaches described by participants to strengthen future emergency response capacity at these critical institutions.

Design, setting, and participants: For this qualitative study, from April through November 2025, key informant interviews were conducted with individuals across SNHs selected to represent a spectrum of SNH types. Thematic analysis of site-level case studies was used to identify cross-cutting and context-specific patterns across 5 domains: load balancing, staffing needs, supply chain, crisis standards of care (CSC), and health care coalitions (HCCs).

Main outcomes and measures: Stakeholder perspectives of pandemic preparedness, response, and recovery were evaluated to understand strategies to mitigate future health care disasters.

Results: Analysis of interviews with 69 individuals from 10 SNH sites identified systemic vulnerabilities across all 5 domains in SNHs. SNHs rarely succeeded in transferring critically ill patients without extensive staff time spent setting up the transfer. SNHs often experienced severe workforce disruptions from limited staff pools and nurse attrition, leaving them dependent on temporary staff at higher costs. Just-in-time personal protective equipment procurement and constricted manufacturing supply chains created supply crises. Few SNHs implemented full CSC, but many worked to find creative solutions to prevent more extensive changes in care standards. Opinions on written CSC were mixed, with some preferring structured frameworks and others preferring flexibility. Experiences with HCCs varied widely, with SNHs embedded in well-resourced HCCs reporting better coordination and support.

Conclusions and relevance: In this qualitative study of SNH preparedness and response, findings indicated that SNHs faced challenges with load balancing, supply chain, staffing, CSC, and HCCs. To address such challenges in the future, SNHs, regional coalitions, and the federal government should implement sustainable changes that can be rapidly brought to bear in an emergency. Potential solutions may have outsized benefit for SNHs; however, such solutions must be designed to be accessible to SNHs and feasible in these settings.

item.title: JAMA Netw Open: Annual Wellness Visits and New Dementia Medication Prescriptions Among US Medicare Beneficiaries

Importance: Medicare annual wellness visits (AWVs) may facilitate early diagnosis of Alzheimer disease and related dementias (ADRDs). However, it remains unclear whether AWVs lead to increased new prescriptions of dementia medications, including N-methyl-d-aspartate receptor antagonists (memantine) and acetylcholinesterase inhibitors (donepezil, rivastigmine, and galantamine).

Objective: To examine the association between incident AWVs and new dementia medication prescriptions.

Design, setting, and participants: This retrospective cohort study used 100% Medicare data for beneficiaries with ADRDs diagnosed from January 1 to December 31, 2018, who had continuous enrollment in Medicare Parts A, B, and D, from 3 years before to 1 year after the index date (January 1, 2018), excluding those enrolled in health maintenance organizations and with prior dementia medication prescriptions. Data analysis was performed from August 2025 to August 2026.

Exposure: Number of AWVs received in the 3 years before the index date (0, 1, 2, or ≥3).

Main outcomes and measures: Receipt of any dementia medication (yes or no).

Results: In this cohort of 799 268 Medicare beneficiaries with ADRDs (mean [SD] age, 82.3 [7.9] years; 64.5% female), 60.8% received no AWVs, 19.2% received 1 AWV, 12.9% received 2 AWVs, and 7.2% received 3 or more AWVs. An interaction between AWVs and prevalent cases of dementia was observed (P for interaction = .009). For both incident and prevalent cases of dementia, a higher rate of dementia medications was associated with a higher number of AWVs, but those with incident dementia cases had larger increases.

Conclusions and relevance: In this cohort study of Medicare beneficiaries with ADRD, an increasing number of AWVs received was associated with higher rates of new dementia medication prescriptions. item.title: JAMA Netw Open: Simpson's Paradox, Amyloid Paradox, and Racial Differences
item.description:
Importance: The underlying mechanisms for the paradox of higher prevalence of dementia but lower prevalence of amyloid positivity in self-identified Black US residents than White US residents remain unknown and are important for designing and analyzing prevention and treatment trials of Alzheimer disease.

Objective: To assess whether the age of mean amyloid onset (AMAO) explains the paradox of the reported racial differences in dementia and amyloid positivity.

Design, setting, and participants: This was a retrospective, multicenter, longitudinal cohort study with harmonized amyloid positron emission tomography (PET) and clinical data from self-identified Black and White individuals who were middle-aged or older across 5 academic institutes in the US conducting studies of memory and aging. The study was conducted from June 2020 to March 2026.

Exposures: Self-identified race, vascular comorbidities, sex, age, educational attainment, and apolipoprotein E ε4 carrier status.

Main outcomes and measures: Amyloid PET centiloid and cognition measured as a global cognitive composite constructed by averaging z scores across at least 6 cognitive tests in self-identified Black and White participants. Both cross-sectional and longitudinal analyses were conducted to compare racial groups in amyloid burden and cognition. Data were also analyzed using propensity score-matching of 2:1 (White:Black) by main covariates.

Results: Of 2653 participants (mean [SD] age, 69.0 [8.8] years; 1574 [59.3%] female), 406 (15.3%) were Black and 2247 (84.7%) were White. Black participants had a delayed AMAO compared with White participants in the unmatched (83.86 [95% CI, 76.55-91.35] years vs 71.38 [95% CI, 67.74-73.17] years; difference, 12.48 [95% CI, 5.03-22.28 years) and covariate-matched (85.17 [95% CI, 80.16-91.38] years vs 72.61 [95% CI, 70.79-74.55] years; difference, 12.57 [95% CI, 7.25-19.54] years) analyses. Although Black participants had a lower overall prevalence of amyloid positivity than White participants (24.1% vs 31.7%, P = .002), they had a higher prevalence of amyloid positivity than White participants in almost every interval of expected years to amyloid onset (EYAO, defined as participants' simple chronological age minus the group-specific AMAO), hence Simpson's paradox, (eg, -15 to -10 years for Black minus White prevalence in the unmatched cohort, 15.30 percentage points [95% Wilson CI, 0.06-0.26]). No significant racial differences were found in the longitudinal rate of amyloid accumulation after adjusting for the covariates either before the AMAO (eg, unmatched cohort Black minus White difference in slope per year, -0.28 [95% CI, -0.64 to 0.08]; P = .13) or after the AMAO (eg, unmatched cohort Black minus White difference in slope, -1.23 [95% CI, -3.05 to 0.60]; P = .17). Black participants had a higher prevalence of vascular comorbidities than White participants (56.9% vs 39.3%; P < .001), and Black but not White participants showed significant cognitive decline before the AMAO (Black minus White difference in slope per year, -0.016 (95% CI, -0.028 to -0.004)]; P = .009).

Conclusions and relevance: This cohort study found that Black participants had delayed AMAO compared with White participants, partially explaining the paradox of the reported racial differences in prevalence of amyloid positivity and dementia. This finding suggests that EYAO may be an important confounder to analyze racial differences and may serve as a better (than age) inclusion or exclusion criterion to improve the representation of Black US residents in clinical trials of Alzheimer disease.

item.description:
Importance: Concerns about adolescent smartphone use and mental health have prompted many schools to implement mobile phone bans, but evidence of their effects remains mixed.

Objective: To examine whether schoolwide mobile phone bans were associated with changes in mental health and associated social and behavioral outcomes among adolescents in Iceland.

Design, setting, and participants: This repeated cross-sectional study used difference-in-differences analyses of data from 70 schools across 3 waves of the nationwide Youth in Iceland school survey. The surveys were administered to adolescents aged 13 to 15 years in February 2016, February 2018, and November 2023. Analyses were conducted from February 1, 2025, to January 30, 2026.

Exposure: Schoolwide mobile phone bans prohibiting student phone use during school hours. Between 2018 and 2023, 22 of 70 schools implemented a phone ban.

Main outcomes and measures: Primary outcomes were depressive symptoms, anxiety, hostility, and mental well-being. Secondary outcomes were perceived peer support, screen use (social media use, gaming alone, gaming with friends, and video watching), and bullying (in person and cyberbullying).

Results: Among 23 938 adolescent observations across the 3 study years, 11 964 (50.0%) were boys; the mean (SD) age was 13.98 (0.82) years. In the postpolicy period from 2018 to 2023, schoolwide mobile phone bans were not associated with meaningful changes in depressive symptoms (β, 0.65 [95% CI, 0.01-1.30]), anxiety (β, 0.21 [95% CI, -0.08 to 0.50]), hostility (β, 0.23 [95% CI, -0.12 to 0.59]), and mental well-being (β, -0.52 [95% CI, -1.08 to 0.03]). Results were similar in gender-stratified analyses and for the secondary outcomes. Sensitivity analyses examining timing of implementation and more stringent phone restriction criteria were consistent with the main findings.

Conclusions and relevance: In this repeated cross-sectional study of adolescents in Iceland, schoolwide mobile phone bans were not associated with meaningful changes in adolescent mental health or related social and behavioral outcomes. These findings suggest that school phone bans implemented in isolation may be insufficient to improve adolescent mental health at the population level.

item.title: Crit Care: Heterogeneous cardiovascular responses to acute mean arterial pressure augmentation in septic shock: the role of ventriculo-arterial coupling and venous return
item.description:
Background: In patients with septic shock, vasopressor-induced mean arterial pressure (MAP) augmentation is commonly used to restore tissue perfusion; however, patients may exhibit divergent cardiovascular responses despite achieving similar arterial pressure targets. We hypothesized that this heterogeneity reflects the differences in ventricular adaptation to increases in arterial load and venous return determinants.

Methods: We conducted a prospective physiological observational study in mechanically ventilated adults with septic shock who underwent transient MAP augmentation from approximately 65 to 85 mmHg after the initial hemodynamic resuscitation. MAP was increased by norepinephrine dose escalation or by adding vasopressin according to clinical judgment. Comprehensive transthoracic echocardiography was performed immediately before and after MAP augmentation. Patients were classified a priori according to the relative changes in cardiac output (CO): flow recruitment (> 15% increase), stable flow (- 15% to + 15%), or flow deterioration (> 15% decrease). Changes in effective arterial elastance (Ea), end-systolic elastance (Ees), VA coupling (Ea/Ees), stroke volume, left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), analogue mean systemic filling pressure (Pmsa), and derived venous return variables were analyzed.

Results: Thirty-two patients were included. Despite comparable increases in MAP, the cardiovascular responses were heterogeneous: 10 patients (31%) exhibited flow recruitment, 17 (53%) maintained a stable flow, and 5 (16%) developed flow deterioration. Patients with flow deterioration showed a greater increase in Ea without a proportional increase in Ees, resulting in worsening VA coupling (ΔEa/Ees + 0.22 IQR [0.01-0.81]), whereas VA coupling remained stable or improved in patients with preserved or increased flow (p = 0.035). Flow deterioration was also associated with reduced LVEF and changes in the derived venous return indices, which may have contributed to the observed reduction in forward flow. Changes in VA coupling correlated with changes in IVCT (ρ = 0.788, p < 0.0001), MPI (ρ = 0.599, p < 0.0003), stroke volume (ρ =-0.418, p = 0.017), and LVEF (ρ=-0.431, p = 0.0139).

Conclusions: Acute MAP augmentation elicits heterogeneous cardiovascular responses in patients with septic shock despite similar increases in arterial pressure. Flow deterioration is characterized by worsening VA coupling, reduced stroke volume, and impaired systolic adaptation, potentially modulated by changes in the derived venous return indices.

item.title: Crit Care: Preserved anabolic skeletal muscle capacity in response to exercise and protein intake after critical illness
item.description:
Background: Low muscle mass and persistent weakness are common after critical illness, but the mechanisms behind impaired recovery are incompletely understood. The aim of this study was to investigate the skeletal muscle anabolic response to combined resistance exercise and protein intake in intensive care unit (ICU) survivors, compared to matched controls without a history of critical illness. We hypothesised that residual anabolic resistance limits muscle regeneration after ICU stay.

Methods: Former patients were enrolled within 3 to 6 months of intensive care unit discharge. Muscle biopsies were obtained before and after resistance exercise using a flywheel leg extension ergometer, combined with ingestion of 24 g hydrolysed protein. Muscle protein fractional synthetic rate was determined from the incorporation of [ring-²H₅]phenylalanine into mixed-muscle protein during a primed continuous intravenous infusion. Anabolic and proteolytic pathways were measured using standard assays. Group-by-time differences were analysed using linear mixed models. The primary comparison was the between-group difference in pre-to-post change in muscle protein synthesis.

Results: Twenty ICU survivors (60 ± 12 years, 30% female, BMI 26.9 (IQR 22.9-28.7), SAPS 3 62.3 ± 15.8) and 20 age- and sex-matched controls were included. ICU survivors had significantly lower quadriceps muscle thickness (p = 0.02) and handgrip strength (p = 0.04) than controls. In ICU survivors, muscle protein synthesis from plasma precursor amino acids was higher at baseline than in controls (0.041%/hour vs. 0.030%/hour, p = 0.009), but increased less (Δ 0.031 vs. Δ 0.040%/hour, p = 0.04). Post-intervention muscle protein synthesis was similar between groups (0.071%/hour vs. 0.070%/hour, p = 0.70). At baseline, ICU survivors showed lower activation of the autophagy-lysosomal pathway. In both groups, the intervention increased anabolic signalling, decreased initiation of autophagy and increased parts of the ubiquitin-proteasome pathway.

Conclusions: In ICU survivors with persistent muscle loss and weakness, the increase in muscle protein synthesis after combined resistance exercise and protein intake was smaller than in controls, in the context of a higher baseline fractional synthetic rate. Post-intervention muscle protein synthesis rates were similar between groups. These findings provide the first mechanistic support for structured exercise-nutrition rehabilitation to promote muscle recovery after critical illness.

Trial registration: This study was prospectively registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05261984), 2022-02-20.

item.title: Am J Respir Crit Care Med: Therapeutic Targeting of the Macrophage YTHDC1/TIGAR/NF-κB Axis Mitigates Pulmonary Hypertension
item.category: American journal of respiratory and critical care medicine
item.description:
Rationale: Immune dysregulation is a pivotal driver of pulmonary hypertension (PH) pathogenesis, yet therapeutic targeting of inflammation has yielded limited clinical success. Although cytosolic RNA-binding proteins are known to regulate immune responses in PH, the specific role of the nuclear m⁶A reader YTHDC1 remains undefined.

Objectives: To elucidate the function of macrophage YTHDC1 in orchestrating inflammatory vascular remodeling during PH.

Methods: Expression profiles of YTHDC1 and TP53-induced glycolysis and apoptosis regulator (TIGAR) were evaluated in human and rodent PH specimens. The mechanistic and therapeutic roles of this axis were assessed using myeloid-specific knockout mice and pharmacological inhibitors (YL-5092, 5Z-7-oxozeaenol) across hypoxia-, SU5416/hypoxia-, and monocrotaline-induced PH models.

Measurements and main results: In patients with idiopathic or connective tissue disease-associated PAH, YTHDC1 and TIGAR expression levels were elevated in pulmonary and circulating macrophages, correlating with disease severity. In murine models, myeloid-specific deletion of Ythdc1 or Tigar conferred profound protection against hypoxia- and SU5416/hypoxia-induced PH. Mechanistically, hypoxia upregulated Ythdc1, which directly bound and stabilized Tigar mRNA. The subsequent accumulation of Tigar protein operated non-enzymatically via a specific domain (residues 152-161) to interact with Tak1, thereby activating the NF-κB cascade, augmenting pro-inflammatory cytokine release, and driving pulmonary artery smooth muscle cell proliferation. Pharmacological inhibition of YTHDC1 (YL-5092) or disruption of the TIGAR-TAK1 interaction (5Z-7-oxozeaenol) effectively attenuated vascular inflammation and mitigated PH progression in diverse rodent models.

Conclusions: The macrophage YTHDC1/TIGAR/NF-κB signaling axis acts as a critical determinant of inflammation and vascular remodeling in PH, representing a potential biomarker and therapeutic target for this disease.

item.title: Chest: Clinical Phenotypes and Prognostic Heterogeneity of Mild-to-Moderate Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease: A Prospective Community-Based Cohort Study
item.description:
Background: The clinical phenotypes, prognosis, and heterogeneity of mild-to-moderate chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) have not been systematically evaluated.

Research question: Do different clinical phenotypes of mild-to-moderate COPD have different prognoses?

Study design and methods: We analysed the baseline and 3-year follow-up data of participants with mild-to-moderate COPD from a prospective community-based cohort study. Mild-to-moderate COPD was defined as a forced expiratory volume in 1 second (FEV1) / forced vital capacity ratio of < 0.70 and FEV1 ≥ 50% of the predicted value. The clinical phenotypes included respiratory symptoms, exacerbation history, emphysema, air trapping, and airway remodelling. Respiratory health outcomes included exacerbations and lung function decline over the 3-year follow-up.

Results: Overall, 806 participants with mild-to-moderate COPD were included, of whom 712 (88%) completed the 3-year follow-up. Participants with mild-to-moderate COPD had more severe emphysema, air trapping, and airway remodelling; increased exacerbation risk; and faster annual FEV1 decline than those with preserved spirometry. The severity of airflow obstruction, respiratory symptoms, emphysema, and air trapping, as well as the eosinophilic phenotype, had low overlap in mild-to-moderate COPD. There was significant individual variation in the annual FEV1 decline rate and exacerbation incidence among participants with mild-to-moderate COPD. Emphysema and air trapping were associated with faster FEV1 decline and higher exacerbation risk. Respiratory symptoms and exacerbations in the previous year were associated with a higher acute exacerbation risk but not with faster lung function decline.

Interpretation: Mild-to-moderate COPD exhibited distinct clinical phenotypes with significant prognostic heterogeneity. Accurate phenotype identification is essential for targeted intervention, clinical precision management, and prognostic improvement.

item.title: Lancet: Izalontamab brengitecan versus platinum-based chemotherapy in EGFR-mutated advanced non-squamous non-small-cell lung cancer after progression on third-generation EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (PANKU-Lung01): a multicentre, randomised, open-label, phase 3 trial in China
item.description:
Background: Izalontamab brengitecan (iza-bren) is a first-in-class bispecific antibody-drug conjugate targeting epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) and human epidermal growth factor receptor 3 (HER3) and has shown antitumour activity in EGFR-mutated non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC). We compared iza-bren with platinum-based chemotherapy in participants with EGFR-mutated advanced non-squamous NSCLC after progression on third-generation EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs).

Methods: In this multicentre, randomised, open-label, phase 3 trial (PANKU-Lung01) conducted at 73 sites in China, eligible participants had EGFR-mutated locally advanced or metastatic non-squamous NSCLC, disease progression after third-generation EGFR TKIs, and had received no previous chemotherapy for advanced disease. Participants were randomly assigned (1:1) to receive iza-bren (2·5 mg/kg intravenously on days 1 and 8 of each 3-week cycle) or pemetrexed plus carboplatin or cisplatin for four to six cycles, with pemetrexed maintenance permitted in participants without progression. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival assessed by blinded independent central review (BICR). The primary analysis included all randomly assigned participants who received at least one dose of study treatment (modified intention-to-treat population). We report the prespecified final progression-free survival and interim overall survival analyses. This trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT06382116.

Findings: Between May 22, 2024, and Sept 1, 2025, we screened 654 participants. After 222 (34%) were excluded, 432 (66%) participants were randomly assigned to iza-bren (n=217 [50%]) or chemotherapy (n=215 [50%]); 422 (98%) received study treatment (216 [51%] in the iza-bren group and 206 [49%] in the chemotherapy group) and comprised the modified intention-to-treat population. At the data cutoff (July 15, 2026; median follow-up for progression-free survival 14·6 months [95% CI 12·9-16·7] in the iza-bren group vs 15·2 months [11·2-18·2] in the chemotherapy group), median BICR-assessed progression-free survival was 11·1 months (9·2-12·7) with iza-bren versus 5·7 months (5·5-5·9) with chemotherapy (hazard ratio [HR] 0·40 [95% CI 0·31-0·51]; one-sided p<0·0001). Treatment-related adverse events of grade 3 or worse occurred in 170 (79%) of 216 participants in the iza-bren group and 128 (62%) of 206 in the chemotherapy group (predominantly haematological); treatment-related adverse events led to permanent discontinuation of at least one study-treatment component in four (2%) participants in each group and treatment-related deaths occurred in one participant in each group. Treatment-related interstitial lung disease occurred in two (1%) participants in the iza-bren group and none in the chemotherapy group.

Interpretation: In participants with EGFR-mutated advanced non-squamous NSCLC after progression on third-generation EGFR TKIs, iza-bren significantly prolonged progression-free survival, although treatment-related adverse events of grade 3 or worse were more frequent than with chemotherapy. To our knowledge, these findings provide the first phase 3 evidence for a bispecific antibody-drug conjugate and support iza-bren as a potential treatment option in this population.

item.title: Lancet: Sacituzumab tirumotecan versus treatment of physician's choice in previously treated endometrial cancer (TroFuse-005/ENGOT-en23/GOG-3095): a randomised, open-label, phase 3 trial
item.description:
Background: Therapeutic options for patients with endometrial cancer who progress after platinum-based chemotherapy and immunotherapy are scarce, and prognosis is poor. Sacituzumab tirumotecan (sac-TMT) is a trophoblast cell-surface antigen 2-directed antibody-drug conjugate with a unique, bifunctional linker that maximises delivery of a belotecan-derived topoisomerase I inhibitor payload to tumour cells. This study aimed to compare sac-TMT with the treatment of physician's choice (TPC) in patients with endometrial cancer who had been previously treated with platinum-based chemotherapy and immunotherapy.

Methods: In this randomised, open-label, phase 3 trial, patients were recruited from 242 gynaecological oncology centres across 31 countries and regions. Participating centres were selected based on established expertise in gynaecological oncology and an adequate volume of potentially eligible patients. Eligible patients were female and aged 18 years or older with histologically confirmed advanced or recurrent endometrial carcinoma or carcinosarcoma, who had received up to three previous lines of therapy, including systemic platinum-based chemotherapy and anti-programmed death 1 or anti-programmed death ligand 1 therapy. Patients were randomly assigned (1:1) via central interactive response technology to receive intravenous sac-TMT (4 mg/kg on days 1 and 15 of each 28-day cycle) or TPC (intravenous doxorubicin 60 mg/m2 every 3 weeks or intravenous paclitaxel 80 mg/m2 on days 1, 8, and 15 of each 28-day cycle). Investigators and patients were not masked to treatment; radiologists performing blinded independent central review were fully masked. Randomisation was stratified by mismatch repair status (deficient vs proficient), trophoblast cell-surface antigen 2 expression by immunohistochemistry (TROP2 EPR20043 Formulation Locked Assay [Roche Tissue Diagnostics, Tucson, AZ, USA]; low [0% to <50% of tumour cells with moderate (2+) or strong (3+) membrane staining intensity] vs medium-high [≥50% tumour cells with moderate (2+) or strong (3+) membrane staining intensity]), number of previous lines of systemic therapy (≤2 vs 3), and baseline disease status per Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors (version 1.1) by blinded independent central review (measurable vs non-measurable). Dual primary endpoints were progression-free survival per Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors (version 1.1) assessed by blinded independent central review and overall survival, analysed in the intention-to-treat population. The data cutoff date was March 23, 2026. Progression-free survival and overall survival were evaluated as dual primary endpoints using a graphical multiple-testing approach with prespecified alpha allocation. Progression-free survival was assessed every 8 weeks through to week 56, then every 12 weeks thereafter; overall survival was assessed continuously. The safety analysis included all randomly assigned patients who received at least one dose of study treatment. For progression-free survival, missing radiographic assessments were handled using prespecified censoring rules; no imputation was performed for missing overall survival or safety data. The trial was registered on ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT06132958) and is ongoing.

Findings: Between Jan 5, 2024, and Sept 17, 2025, 776 patients were randomly assigned to sac-TMT (n=386) or TPC (n=390). 384 (99%) of 386 patients in the sac-TMT group and 367 (94%) of 390 in the TPC group received at least one dose of study treatment. At data cutoff, median follow-up was 14·0 months (IQR 11·0-16·9). Median progression-free survival was 7·2 months (95% CI 5·6-7·6) in the sac-TMT group and 3·9 months (3·7-5·3) in the TPC group (hazard ratio 0·59 [95% CI 0·50-0·70]; p<0·0001) and median overall survival was 19·0 months (16·1-not reached) in the sac-TMT group and 12·1 months (11·0-15·2) in the TPC group (0·68 [0·55-0·84]; p=0·0001). 265 (69%) of 384 patients in the sac-TMT group and 210 (57%) of 367 in the TPC group had a grade 3 or higher adverse event. Serious adverse events were reported in 133 (35%) patients in the sac-TMT group and 117 (32%) patients in the TPC group. Treatment-related adverse events led to death in three (<1%) patients in the sac-TMT group and three (<1%) in the TPC group.

Interpretation: Sac-TMT significantly improved progression-free survival and overall survival versus TPC in patients with advanced or recurrent endometrial cancer previously treated with platinum-based chemotherapy and immunotherapy. These findings support sac-TMT as a new standard of care for patients with endometrial cancer who have received chemotherapy and immunotherapy and have few effective treatment options.

item.title: Lancet: Izalontamab brengitecan for HR+/HER2- breast cancer in China (PANKU-Breast01): a randomised, phase 3 trial
item.description:
Background: Patients with heavily pretreated hormone receptor-positive and human epidermal growth factor receptor 2-negative (HR+/HER2-) breast cancer have few treatment options. Izalontamab brengitecan (iza-bren) is a first-in-class, epidermal growth factor receptor and HER3 bispecific antibody-drug conjugate that contains a potent topoisomerase I inhibitor payload (Ed-04). The aim of PANKU-Breast01 was to compare the efficacy and safety of iza-bren versus chemotherapy in patients with pretreated HR+/HER2- breast cancer.

Methods: In this randomised, phase 3, open-label, multicentre study in 72 hospitals in China, patients with HR+/HER2- breast cancer who had disease progression after endocrine therapy, cyclin-dependent kinase (CDK) 4/6 inhibitors, and one or two lines of chemotherapy were randomly assigned (1:1) to iza-bren (2·5 mg/kg, administered by intravenous infusion on day 1 and day 8 every 3 weeks) or physician's choice chemotherapy (eribulin, 1·4 mg/m2; vinorelbine, 25 mg/m2; or gemcitabine, 1000 mg/m2, all administered by intravenous infusion on day 1 and day 8 every 3 weeks; or capecitabine, 1000-1250 mg/m2, administered orally twice daily on days 1-14 of each 3-week cycle). Stratified block randomisation was performed by an independent vendor using an interactive web response system, with stratification factors of number of previous lines of chemotherapy, CNS metastasis, and HER2 expression status. Patients, investigators, and site personnel involved in patient care and performing trial procedures were not masked to treatment assignment. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival assessed by Blinded Independent Central Review per RECIST (version 1.1) in the modified intention-to-treat population, which consisted of all randomly assigned participants who had at least one dose of study drug. Median progression-free survival was estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method and hazard ratios (HRs) were calculated using a stratified Cox proportional hazards model. The trial was registered at ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT06343948, and is closed to recruitment.

Findings: Between April 24, 2024, and June 6, 2025, 560 patients were screened, 177 were excluded, and 383 patients were randomly assigned and treated (190 were assigned to the iza-bren group and 193 were assigned to the chemotherapy group). All 383 participants in the study were female and of Chinese ethnicity. Median age was 54·0 years (IQR 47·0-60·0). At data cutoff (July 21, 2026), median follow-up for progression-free survival was 15·2 months (95% CI 13·9-16·8). Iza-bren significantly improved progression-free survival versus chemotherapy (log-rank p<0·0001), and median progression-free survival assessed by Blinded Independent Central Review was 8·2 months (95% CI 6·9-8·6) versus 4·0 months (2·9-4·3; HR 0·41 [95% CI 0·33-0·53]). Grade 3 or higher treatment-related adverse events occurred in 162 (85%) patients in the iza-bren group versus 127 (66%) patients in the chemotherapy group, and haematological adverse events were the most common in both groups. For the treatment of haematological adverse events, 138 (73%) patients in the iza-bren group received platelet-elevating agents, 28 (15%) patients in the iza-bren group received platelet transfusion, and 18 patients (10%) in the iza-bren group received a blood transfusion. Two patients in the iza-bren group died due to treatment-related adverse events.

Interpretation: Iza-bren showed a significant improvement in progression-free survival versus chemotherapy in patients with HR+/HER2- breast cancer previously treated with endocrine therapy, CDK4/6 inhibitors, and one or two lines of chemotherapy (including taxanes). The overall survival data were immature, and an overall survival benefit has not been established. These results suggest that iza-bren could be a new treatment option for this population in China; however, further evaluation of iza-bren in global populations and in earlier lines of therapy for HER2-negative breast cancer is warranted.

item.title: Lancet: First-line pembrolizumab versus carboplatin plus paclitaxel in participants with mismatch repair-deficient advanced or recurrent endometrial cancer (KEYNOTE-C93/GOG-3064/ENGOT-en15): interim analysis of a multicentre, open-label, randomised, active-comparator controlled, phase 3 trial
item.description:
Background: A need exists for first-line chemotherapy-free options in advanced or recurrent endometrial cancer. We therefore assessed the efficacy, quality of life, and safety of first-line pembrolizumab versus carboplatin plus paclitaxel in mismatch repair-deficient (dMMR) advanced or recurrent endometrial cancer.

Methods: The KEYNOTE-C93/GOG-3064/ENGOT-en15 multicentre, open-label, randomised, active-comparator controlled, phase 3 trial was conducted at 122 centres in 24 countries in the Americas, Asia, Europe, and Oceania. Adult participants (≥18 years) with inoperable, stage III or IV, persistent, advanced, or recurrent dMMR endometrial cancer were randomly assigned 1:1 to intravenous pembrolizumab 400 mg every 6 weeks for up to 18 cycles or intravenous carboplatin area under the curve 5 mg/mL or 6 mg/mL per min plus paclitaxel 175 mg/m2 on day 1 of each 3-week cycle for six cycles. Randomisation was stratified by disease status, histology, and previous receipt of (neo)adjuvant chemotherapy. Primary endpoints were progression-free survival per RECIST version 1.1, by blinded independent central review, and overall survival. This trial is registered at ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT05173987, and is ongoing.

Findings: Between Feb 22, 2022, and Dec 12, 2023, 299 participants were assigned to pembrolizumab (n=149) or carboplatin plus paclitaxel (n=150). At the cutoff for the prespecified interim analysis in the intention-to-treat population (April 24, 2026), median progression-free survival was 38·2 months (95% CI 17·9 months-not reached) in the pembrolizumab group versus 8·4 months (6·8-10·4) in the carboplatin plus paclitaxel group (hazard ratio [HR] 0·57, 95% CI 0·42-0·79; p=0·0002). Estimated progression-free survival was 75% (95% CI 67-81) versus 76% (68-82) at 6 months, 67% (59-74) versus 40% (32-48) at 12 months, and 53% (44-61) versus 30% (22-38) at 36 months. The prespecified statistical significance criterion for overall survival was not met at the interim analysis (medians not reached; HR 0·77, 95% CI 0·52-1·15; p=0·10). Grade 3 or higher treatment-related adverse events occurred in 27 (18%) of 149 participants in the pembrolizumab group and 73 (51%) of 144 in the carboplatin plus paclitaxel group. Treatment-related adverse events of any grade that occurred in at least 25% of participants in either group included alopecia (three [2%] of 149 in the pembrolizumab group, 72 [50%] of 144 in the carboplatin plus paclitaxel group), anaemia (seven [5%], 71 [49%]), nausea (seven [5%], 41 [28%]), decreased neutrophil count (five [3%], 40 [28%]), peripheral neuropathy (none, 38 [26%]), and fatigue (20 [13%], 37 [26%]). Treatment-related adverse events led to treatment discontinuation in 14 (9%) of 149 participants in the pembrolizumab group and 21 (15%) of 144 participants in the carboplatin plus paclitaxel group; they resulted in death in two participants in the pembrolizumab group (hepatic failure and bacterial meningitis [n=1 each]) and one participant in the carboplatin plus paclitaxel group (pulmonary embolism).

Interpretation: First-line pembrolizumab showed a statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvement in progression-free survival, with lower frequency of overall and grade 3 or above treatment-related adverse events. The study did not compare pembrolizumab monotherapy with the current standard of care (immunotherapy plus chemotherapy).

item.title: Lancet: Ruzaltatug rezetecan versus chemotherapy for EGFR-mutated advanced non-small-cell lung cancer progressing after EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor therapy (HERON-Lung01): interim analysis of a randomised, open-label, phase 3 trial in China
item.description:
Background: Ruzaltatug rezetecan is a novel HER3-directed antibody-drug conjugate that has shown promising antitumour activity and manageable safety in pretreated EGFR-.mutated non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) in a phase 1 trial. We aimed to compare the efficacy and safety of ruzaltatug rezetecan with chemotherapy in patients with EGFR-mutated advanced NSCLC that had progressed after EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) therapy.

Methods: HERON-Lung01 is a randomised, open-label, phase 3 trial conducted at 62 sites in China. Eligible patients were aged 18-75 years, with locally advanced or metastatic non-squamous NSCLC harbouring an EGFR activating mutation (exon 19 deletion or L858R mutation), and had progressed during or after EGFR-TKI therapy. Patients were randomly assigned (1:1) to receive ruzaltatug rezetecan 8·0 mg/kg or chemotherapy comprising pemetrexed 500 mg/m2 plus carboplatin (area under the curve 5) or cisplatin 75 mg/m2 for four cycles, followed by maintenance pemetrexed. All treatments were administered intravenously on day 1 of each 3-week cycle. Block randomisation was stratified by presence of brain metastases, EGFR mutation subtype, and use of a first-line third-generation EGFR-TKI. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival (PFS), as assessed by blinded independent central review (BICR), in the intention-to-treat population. This trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT06671379). Recruitment is complete, with the trial ongoing.

Findings: Between Nov 29, 2024, and Jan 29, 2026, 498 patients were randomly assigned to receive ruzaltatug rezetecan (n=250) or chemotherapy (n=248). The median age was 60·0 years (IQR 54·0-68·0); 276 (55%) patients were female and 222 (45%) male. At the prespecified interim PFS analysis, median follow-up was 7·7 months (95% CI 7·1-8·3). BICR-assessed PFS was significantly longer with ruzaltatug rezetecan than with chemotherapy (median 8·3 months vs 5·4 months; hazard ratio 0·47 [95% CI 0·36-0·60]; one-sided p<0·0001). item.description:
Background: Stroke mimics present with acute neurological symptoms resembling stroke and remain a major diagnostic challenge in the emergency department (ED). Early differentiation from true stroke is important for timely treatment and appropriate resource utilization.

Objective: To determine the prevalence, etiologies, and clinical predictors of stroke mimics among patients presenting to the ED with suspected acute stroke within 9 h of symptom onset.

Methods: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of adults who presented to the ED of Srinagarind Hospital, Thailand, between January 2021 and December 2024. Eligible patients were aged ≥18 years, had suspected acute stroke within 9 h of symptom onset, and were triaged through the institutional Stroke Fast-Track protocol. Demographic characteristics, comorbidities, presenting symptoms, physical examination findings, and neuroimaging results were extracted from electronic medical records. Attending neurologists determined the final diagnoses. Univariate and multivariable logistic regression analyses identified factors independently associated with stroke mimics.

Results: Among 1615 patients, 347 (21.5%; 95% confidence interval [CI], 19.5-23.5%) were diagnosed with stroke mimics. Seizure-related disorders were the most common etiology (13.8%), followed by cardiovascular and cerebrovascular non-stroke conditions (11.2%) and infectious or inflammatory diseases (10.1%). In multivariable analysis, younger age, male sex, a history of migraine, psychiatric disorders, and epilepsy, along with lower diastolic blood pressure and higher heart rate, were independently associated with stroke mimics. Presenting features independently associated with stroke mimics included altered consciousness (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 1.71; 95% CI, 1.25-2.33), seizure (aOR 2.68; 95% CI, 1.79-4.00), vertigo (aOR 1.85; 95% CI, 1.28-2.65), and fever (aOR 3.10; 95% CI, 1.36-7.12). Conversely, limb weakness and speech disturbance were independently associated with confirmed stroke.

Conclusion: Stroke mimics accounted for 21.5% of suspected acute stroke presentations in the ED. Altered consciousness, seizure, vertigo, and fever were independently associated with stroke mimics, whereas limb weakness and speech disturbance favored confirmed stroke.

item.title: J Emerg Med: Evaluating Culturally Tailored Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR) Training in Racial and Ethnically Diverse Communities
item.description:
Background: Bystander cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) is a critical determinant of survival following out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA). However, racial and ethnic minority populations in the United States are less likely to receive bystander CPR and experience disproportionately poorer outcomes.

Study objectives: The objective of this study was to pilot and evaluate the feasibility of a culturally tailored hands-only CPR curriculum and assess changes in self-reported confidence and perceived difficulty of CPR among Indian American, Chinese American, and African American participants.

Methods: We conducted a single-cohort pre-post study among three groups. Community-specific focus groups informed cultural adaptations to a standard emergency services hands-only CPR curriculum, and trainings were delivered at Hindu temples, Chinese language schools, and African American churches. Primary outcomes, measured by 10-point Likert scales, were changes in confidence in four main CPR skills and perceived difficulty of CPR.

Results: The study included 104 participants: 47 (45%) Indian American, 23 (22%) Chinese American, and 34 (33%) African American participants. Confidence increased across the four main CPR skills, with the largest improvements observed in the connect an automated external defibrillator (AED) skill (+4.5; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 3.80-5.22). Perceived difficulty of CPR also decreased (-2.65; 95% CI: 1.97-3.33).

Conclusion: This pilot study provides preliminary evidence for the feasibility and acceptability of culturally tailored hands-only CPR training in community settings, with participants reporting improved confidence and reduced perceived difficulty of CPR after training. These exploratory findings warrant further evaluation in adequately powered comparative studies to determine whether cultural tailoring offers benefit beyond standard CPR instruction for racial and ethnic minority communities and can contribute to reducing disparities in cardiac arrest outcomes.

item.title: J Emerg Med: Epidemiology of Nephrolithiasis Among United States Emergency Departments Over a 9-Year Period
item.description:
Background: Nephrolithiasis is a common emergency department (ED) presentation, yet contemporary national data on management trends are limited.

Objectives: To characterize recent trends in diagnostic evaluation, management, and disposition for adult ED patients with nephrolithiasis.

Methods: This cross-sectional study analyzed United States ED encounters from January 1, 2016 to December 31, 2024 using the Epic Cosmos database, including all adult patients (≥18 years) with an ICD-10 diagnosis of nephrolithiasis. Outcomes included hospital admission, imaging utilization, urine culture collection, medication administration, discharge prescription, and procedural intervention. Descriptive statistics were utilized to characterize the study population. To account for the longitudinal expansion of the database, time-stratified odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated using the general ED population as a background comparator. Significance of temporal shifts was assessed using Cochran-Armitage tests.

Results: Of 248,564,812 ED encounters, 2,762,879 (1.1%) were for nephrolithiasis. Hospital admission rates increased from 8.9% in 2016 to 12.7% in 2024. Computed tomography (CT) utilization increased (73.8-89.8%), outpacing general ED trends (OR 27.2-45.6), while ultrasound declined (5.8-3.8%). In the ED, opioid use fell (61.5-49.7%), exceeding background reductions (OR 6.6-4.8), while ketorolac was the most common analgesic administered (61.6%). Tamsulosin remained the top discharge prescription (47.2%). Procedural interventions were uncommon, though stent placement increased from 3.0% to 6.8%.

Conclusions: We identified rising hospital admission rates and an increase in CT utilization, while there was a decline in ultrasound. This divergence between practice patterns and evidence-based guidelines, highlights critical opportunities for quality improvement.

item.title: Ann Intern Med: Laparoscopic Versus Open Liver Resection for Colorectal Liver Metastases : An Individual Participant Data Meta-analysis of Four Randomized Clinical Trials
item.description:
Background: Randomized clinical trials (RCTs) have compared laparoscopic liver resection (LLR) and open liver resection (OLR) for colorectal liver metastases (CRLM); however, long-term outcomes and subgroup effects have not been comprehensively evaluated.

Purpose: To compare postoperative and long-term oncologic outcomes after LLR versus OLR for CRLM using individual participant data from RCTs.

Data sources: PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials were searched from database inception through March 2025 for RCTs comparing LLR and OLR for CRLM.

Study selection: Eligible studies were RCTs comparing LLR and OLR for CRLM.

Data extraction: Individual participant data, including unpublished data, were obtained from trial investigators of all 4 published RCTs.

Data synthesis: Analyses used a modified intention-to-treat approach and 1-stage individual participant data meta-analysis (IPDMA) with trial-adjusted regression models and g-computation to estimate standardized treatment effects across outcomes, with 95% CIs obtained by nonparametric bootstrap resampling. Prespecified subgroup analyses assessed heterogeneity of treatment effect for the primary outcome. A total of 761 patients were included (laparoscopic, n = 384; open, n = 377). Postoperative morbidity was lower in patients assigned to laparoscopic surgery compared with open surgery (19% vs. 27%). Among patients who received preoperative systemic therapy, morbidity did not differ between groups (25% vs. 24%). Ninety-day mortality was 1.8% after LLR and 0.8% after OLR. After a median follow-up of 93 months, overall survival and disease-free survival did not differ between groups.

Limitation: Analyses were limited to variables available across all studies.

Conclusion: In this IPDMA of all published RCTs in the field, LLR for CRLM was associated with lower postoperative morbidity than OLR, with similar long-term oncologic outcomes.

item.title: Ann Intern Med: Obesity and Cancer Risk in Young Adults in Korea : A Nationwide Health Screening Cohort Study
item.description:
Background: Obesity and early-onset cancer are both increasing among young adults, yet evidence remains limited.

Objective: To assess associations between obesity and early-onset cancer risk in young adults.

Design: Nationwide population-based cohort study.

Setting: Korean National Health Insurance Service database, 2009 to 2021.

Patients: 6 313 338 adults aged 20 to 39 years without prior cancer, from a national health screening program.

Measurements: Body mass index (BMI) was categorized into 5 groups (underweight to class II obesity) according to Asian-specific criteria. The outcome was incident cancer.

Results: During a mean follow-up of 11.2 years, 151 893 cancer cases occurred. Ten-year cumulative incidence ranged from 1.84% (95% CI, 1.83% to 1.86%) in the normal-weight group to 2.24% (CI, 2.22% to 2.27%) in class I obesity and 2.62% (CI, 2.56% to 2.68%) in class II obesity, with absolute risk differences of 0.40% (CI, 0.39% to 0.41%) and 0.78% (CI, 0.73% to 0.82%). The relative association was more pronounced in men, and absolute risk differences were greater in women. In combined BMI-waist circumference analyses, people with class I obesity based on BMI and with abdominal obesity had higher 10-year cumulative incidence (2.45% [CI, 2.41% to 2.50%]) than those without abdominal obesity (2.13% [CI, 2.10% to 2.16%]), exceeding that of those with class II obesity without abdominal obesity (2.20% [CI, 2.03% to 2.36%]). The highest cumulative incidence was observed for thyroid, endometrial, and ovarian cancer. Obesity was not associated with higher risk for breast cancer diagnosed by age 50 years.

Limitations: Observational design; nonrepresentative sample limited to screening participants; and unmeasured confounding, including smoking burden.

Conclusion: Obesity in young Korean adults, measured by BMI and waist circumference, is associated with higher early-onset cancer risk persisting into midlife, with patterns varying by cancer type. Early weight management may be important for prevention.

item.title: Ann Intern Med: Impact of Unrestricted Artificial Intelligence Scribe Deployment in a Single Health System on Clinician Workload and Productivity : A Quality Improvement Study
item.description:
Background: Ambient artificial intelligence (AI) medical scribes may reduce documentation burden and clinician burnout. Whether use intensity drives benefits remains uncertain.

Objective: To evaluate the association between AI scribe (Heidi) enrollment and documentation burden and whether changes differ by use intensity.

Design: Retrospective quality improvement study using an interrupted time series (ITS) indexed on each clinician's enrollment month adjusted for patient demographics and visit complexity. A secondary 3-group ITS compared enrolled nonusers, low users, and high users.

Setting: 14-hospital health system in Boston, Massachusetts.

Participants: 902 outpatient clinicians enrolled in Heidi; 605 users and 297 enrolled nonusers.

Intervention: Heidi enrollment after system-wide implementation beginning January 2025.

Measurements: The primary outcome was note-active time. Secondary outcomes included same-day and after-hours note closures, note length, and work relative value units (wRVUs).

Results: 1 637 227 encounters had notes authored by enrolled clinicians between 1 July 2024 and 31 January 2026. Enrollment was associated with an immediate reduction in note-active time (-1.21 minutes [95% CI, -1.74 to -0.68 minutes]), with larger reductions among high users (-2.50 minutes [CI, -3.55 to -1.45 minutes]) than nonusers (difference, -2.20 minutes [CI, -3.46 to -0.95 minutes]) and low users (difference, -1.72 minutes [CI, -3.03 to -0.40 minutes]). High users had greater increases in note length than nonusers (difference, +170.90 characters [CI, 21.07 to 320.70 characters]) and low users (difference, +270.70 characters [CI, 131.04 to 410.36 characters]). No differences were observed in same-day closure, after-hours closure, or wRVUs.

Limitation: Observational design with potential unmeasured confounding; inability to distinguish AI-scribed from clinician-authored notes postenrollment.

Conclusion: Heidi enrollment was associated with reductions in documentation time and increases in note length, concentrated among high users. Enrollment was not associated with improvements in same-day, after-hours note closures, or wRVUs.

item.title: Intensive Care Med: European Society of Intensive Care Medicine consensus statement on human-centred partnership in the intensive care unit
item.description:
A human-centred partnership in the intensive care unit (ICU) aims to integrate person-centred care, communication, emotional support, equity, and collaboration into ICU environments. The European Society of Intensive Care Medicine (ESICM) developed a consensus statement on human-centred partnership in the ICU following a systematic, multi-phase, evidence-informed methodology incorporating the views of ICU professionals, academics, and patient and family representatives. This international multidisciplinary panel of 46 members conducted rapid reviews addressing 20 Population, Intervention, Comparator, Outcomes (PICO) questions across six domains: person-centred care; communication and transparency; emotional well-being; equity, diversity, and inclusion; ICU environment; technology and innovation. Based on the evidence synthesis, 53 draft statements were developed and evaluated through a two-round eDelphi study. The final set of statements was discussed and ratified at an expert consensus meeting with the initial panel of experts and with patients and family representatives. A total of 201 international stakeholders participated in round 1 and 149 in round 2. Members of the expert consensus meeting ultimately endorsed 43 consensus statements. Key recommendations supported flexible family visitation, structured interdisciplinary communication, empathy-based staff training, psychological support for patients and ICU professionals, culturally responsive care, environmental interventions to improve sleep and reduce delirium, and the integration of digital supported technologies. The consensus statement on human-centred partnership in the ICU provides a comprehensive framework for clinicians with evidence-informed directions to deliver high-quality practice across diverse ICU settings. By prioritising person-centred care, communication, inclusivity, and well-being alongside responsible technological innovation, the experiences and outcomes of patients, families, and ICU professionals may improve.

item.title: JAMA Intern Med: Preoperative Medicine for the Internal Medicine Clinician: A Review
item.description:
Importance: Internal medicine clinicians are often involved in preoperative evaluation and counseling for their patients, yet explicit training and exposure opportunities in perioperative medicine are limited. Beyond providing clearance for surgery or anesthesiology care, preoperative medical care presents an opportunity for clinicians to use clinical skills, evidence-based medicine, and skilled communication with patients and caregivers to maximize benefit and safety during a planned surgery. This review explores foundations of preoperative medicine to help internal medicine clinicians contribute to safe, high-value, patient-centered preoperative care, including an overview of high-yield resources and professional society guidelines.

Observations: Delivery of preoperative medical care requires history, physical examination, interpretation of diagnostic test results, and clinical reasoning, supported by a scaffold of published guidelines and evidence. The preoperative examination begins with carefully reviewing the status of known health conditions and current medications in the context of operative risk, which can lead to recommendations for risk reduction and inform the need for further testing. Further, clinicians should also investigate undifferentiated symptoms and other preoperative risk factors that arise during the evaluation, such as exertional dyspnea and examination findings of volume overload. Finally, the preoperative assessment should include communication of individualized risks and benefits of the planned surgery, engaging the patient in shared decision-making around preoperative preparation. A comprehensive preoperative evaluation can not only help patients prepare for surgery but also inform care provided by the surgical and anesthesiology teams during and postoperatively.

Conclusions and relevance: Using an evidence-informed, stepwise approach, internal medicine clinicians can have a beneficial impact on the preoperative course for their patients.
