item.title: JAMA Intern Med: Preoperative Intranasal Oxytocin and Probable Acute Stress Disorder After Traumatic Fracture Surgery: A Randomized Clinical Trial
item.description:
Importance: Acute stress disorder (ASD) is a common and debilitating psychological sequela following traumatic fracture surgery, adversely affecting recovery and predicting chronic posttraumatic stress disorder. Effective pharmacological prevention strategies are currently lacking.

Objective: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of a single preoperative dose of intranasal oxytocin for the prevention of screening-positive probable ASD in patients undergoing traumatic fracture surgery.

Design, setting, and participants: This single-center, prospective, double-blind, placebo-controlled randomized clinical trial was conducted at the General Hospital of Western Theater Command in China. From April 2024 to April 2025, adult patients scheduled for traumatic fracture surgery were enrolled and randomized.

Interventions: Participants were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to either receive intranasal oxytocin, 40 IU, or an equivalent volume of intranasal saline placebo 10 minutes before the induction of anesthesia.

Main outcomes and measures: The primary outcome was the cumulative incidence of a first screening-positive probable ASD within 3 days postoperatively, defined by a Stanford Acute Stress Reaction Questionnaire (SAS-RQ) score of 40 or higher. Key secondary outcomes included the Connor-Davidson Resilience Scale (CD-RISC), the Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS), and salivary malondialdehyde, cortisol, and superoxide dismutase levels.

Results: A total of 328 patients were randomized (164 to the saline group and 164 to the oxytocin group) and included in the intention-to-treat analysis. The median (IQR) age of all participants was 50 (34-57) years; 210 participants (64.0%) were male, and 118 participants (36.0%) were female. The 3-day cumulative incidence of screening-positive probable ASD was 26 of 164 (15.9%) in the oxytocin group vs 50 of 164 (30.5%) in the saline group (risk difference, -14.6 percentage points [pp]; 95% CI, -23.5 to -5.5 pp; risk ratio, 0.52; 95% CI, 0.34-0.79). In the prespecified Cox model, preoperative oxytocin was associated with a lower hazard of a positive screening result during follow-up (adjusted hazard ratio, 0.45; 95% CI, 0.27-0.75). Exploratory analyses suggested improved psychological outcomes and directionally consistent alterations in stress biomarker trajectories. No serious adverse events were observed.

Conclusions and relevance: In this randomized clinical trial, preoperative intranasal oxytocin is associated with a lower cumulative incidence of probable ASD after traumatic fracture surgery. These findings suggest that intranasal oxytocin may represent a feasible perioperative preventive strategy; however, these exploratory mechanistic insights and long-term safety profile warrant further investigation.

Objective: To ascertain the association of prison incarceration with cancer outcomes, and to inform potential public health interventions.

Design, setting, and participants: This cohort study used state cancer registry data on patients with cancer diagnosed in California and Massachusetts between January 1, 2010, and December 31, 2019. Identifiers of persons incarcerated in California and Massachusetts state prisons during this study period were linked to cancer registry data to identify incarceration status at diagnosis. Data analysis was performed between March 2023 and August 2025.

Main outcomes and measures: Cancer incidence, which was calculated as standardized incidence ratios (SIRs) relative to never-incarcerated patients. Objective: To examine associations between genetic counselor (GC) biases (implicit and/or explicit prejudice and stereotyping) and patient-centered outcomes in cancer genetic counseling.

Design, setting, and participants: This is a cohort study of patient-clinician communication during cancer genetic counseling focusing on hereditary cancer risk assessment. Data were collected at 2 comprehensive cancer centers in the South and Midwest, from August 3, 2023, to July 30, 2025.

Exposure: At baseline, GCs completed measures of implicit prejudice (Race Implicit Association Test), implicit stereotyping (Medical Cooperativeness Implicit Association Test), explicit prejudice (feeling thermometer), and explicit stereotyping (general and medical-context stereotype subscales).

Differences between Black and White patients were evaluated using Welch t test for continuous variables and χ2 or Fisher exact test for categorical variables. Importance: Cancer is the leading cause of death in prison. Limited literature suggests cancer screening rates in prison are low, but population-level screening data in prisons are scarce.

Objective: To determine screening rates for 5 cancer types, identify individual and incarceration characteristics associated with receipt of screening, and characterize outcomes for screen-detectable cancers in California prisons.

Design, setting, and participants: This cohort study included individuals incarcerated in California state prisons who were eligible for breast, cervical, colorectal, liver, or lung cancer screening between January 1, 2014, and June 30, 2023. Incarceration data were linked to state cancer registry data from 2014 to 2021 to identify screen-detectable cancers diagnosed in the study population. Analyses were conducted between August 2024 and July 2025.

Exposures: Receipt of screening within 3 months before a cancer diagnosis.

Main outcomes and measures: Receipt of cancer screening; screening rates; and cancer diagnosis, stage, and survival were calculated. Multivariable models evaluated characteristics associated with screening receipt and associations between screening receipt and stage at diagnosis and survival, with adjustment for demographic and incarceration characteristics.

Results: The study included 106 352 incarcerated individuals (median [IQR] age at first eligibility, 50 [47-55] years; 86 559 males [81.4%]). By June 30, 2023 (data cutoff), 89.4%, 81.2%, 80.0%, 70.1%, and 76.0% of individuals were up-to-date with screening for breast, colorectal, cervical, lung, and liver cancer screening, respectively. Characteristics associated with higher likelihood of ever receiving screening included mental health service use, prison security level 3 or 4, recent change in primary care practitioner, and incarceration within the past year before screening eligibility. Of 812 patients with screening data, 92 (11.3%) were diagnosed with screen-detectable cancer before they met eligibility for screening, including 56 with liver cancer. A total of 392 screening-eligible patients (48.3%) were diagnosed with screen-detectable cancer while in prison during the study period. Approximately 71% of patients received screening within 3 months before diagnosis, which was associated with lower odds of stage IV disease at diagnosis (odds ratio, 0.44; 95% CI, 0.23-0.85) and better survival (hazard ratio, 0.63; 95% CI, 0.44-0.88); rates of stage IV cancer were lower for individuals with recent screening than those without recent screening (10.0% vs 21.0%).

Conclusions and relevance: In this cohort study of incarcerated individuals in California prisons, screening rates were high and associated with early-stage cancer diagnoses, suggesting that effective cancer screening is achievable in prison settings. Future work should examine whether increased screening ameliorates incarceration-related cancer disparities.

item.description:
Importance: Food insecurity is associated with adverse health and affects approximately 1 in 5 US medical students. A recent multi-institutional study found food insecurity in 14% of graduate medical education trainees using a 2-item screen; prevalence by the 10-item US Department of Agriculture Adult Food Security Survey Module remains poorly characterized.

Objective: To estimate reported food insecurity prevalence among resident physicians and clinical fellows and identify affected subgroups and barriers.

Design, setting, and participants: In this cross-sectional, anonymous electronic survey at the Yale New Haven Health System, all physicians in accredited postgraduate training were eligible (approximately 600). The survey was fielded August 7, 2023, to May 19, 2026, and responses arrived through November 2025 (121 of 165 [73%] in 2023).

Exposures: Year of training (including postgraduate year 1 [PGY-1] status) and self-reported barriers to obtaining food.

Main outcomes and measures: Food insecurity, a score of 3 or higher on the 10-item US Department of Agriculture module; prevalences and associations reported with 95% CIs.

Results: Of approximately 600 eligible trainees, 165 (28%) participated; 164 had complete food security data (53 PGY-1, 34 PGY-2, 23 PGY-3, 32 PGY-4, 22 other, including fellows). Overall, 50 of 164 respondents (30.5%; 95% CI, 24.0%-37.9%) met criteria for food insecurity. PGY-1 prevalence (24 of 53 [45.3%]) was approximately twice that of later years (26 of 111 [23.4%]; odds ratio [OR], 2.71; 95% CI, 1.35-5.43; P = .004). Lack of money was associated with food insecurity (45 of 60 [75.0%] vs 4 of 100 [4.0%]; OR, 72.00; 95% CI, 22.61-229.30; P < .001), whereas lack of time was not (OR, 1.24; 95% CI, 0.61-2.49; P = .55). PGY-1 trainees more often endorsed lack of money (27 of 52 [51.9%] vs 33 or 108 [30.6%]; OR, 2.45; 95% CI, 1.24-4.85; P = .009). Prevalence by specialty ranged from 5 of 26 (19.2%) to 5 of 10 (50.0%) (P = .24).

Conclusions and relevance: In this cross-sectional study of 164 resident physicians and clinical fellows, approximately one-third of respondents reported food insecurity, with the highest burden among PGY-1 trainees, whose recall window spanned the transition from medical school into residency, and an association with lack of money. item.title: JAMA Netw Open: Stroke and Bleeding Risk in Long-Term Care Residents With Atrial Fibrillation Who Discontinue Anticoagulation
item.description:
Importance: Atrial fibrillation (AF) leads to more than 100 000 cases of stroke yearly and is particularly prevalent in long-term care (LTC) residents. Anticoagulation (AC) is the mainstay of stroke prevention, but given its risks, clinicians and residents may consider discontinuation at the time of LTC entry.

Objective: To estimate the association between AC discontinuation and stroke and bleeding risk among LTC residents with AF.

Design, setting, and participants: This comparative effectiveness research study with target trial emulation used claims data (2020-2021) from LTC facilities in the US serving Medicare beneficiaries. Medicare beneficiaries with AF receiving AC who entered LTC between April 1 and December 31, 2020, were included; those with additional indications for AC, including prosthetic heart valve or venous thromboembolism, were excluded. Analysis was performed in August 2026.

Exposure: Discontinuer vs continuer assignment.

Main outcomes and measures: The main outcomes were stroke (including ischemic stroke, transient ischemic attack, and systemic embolism) and bleeding, assessed using Medicare claims. A target trial emulation was conducted with clone censor weighting (CCW) analysis. Specifically, eligible LTC residents were assigned (cloned) to each of 2 strategies: AC discontinuation or AC continuation. Clones were then censored when they deviated from their assigned strategy, and inverse probability of censoring weighting was applied to address informative censoring: residents who deviated differing systematically from those who did not. Subdistribution hazard ratios (sHRs) for stroke and bleeding were then calculated to account for competing mortality and a cause-specific hazard ratio (HR) for death.

Results: This study included 15 426 LTC residents (mean [SD] age, 82.6 [7.6] years). Most were female (62.6%). AC discontinuers had 187 strokes, 297 bleeding events, and 3684 deaths over a mean (SD) of 128.9 (177.9) days. AC continuers had 321 strokes, 493 bleeding events, and 5475 deaths over a mean (SD) of 279.6 (204.9) days. Discontinuers had similar stroke risk (sHR, 1.07; 95% CI, 0.93-1.23) and bleeding risk (sHR, 1.02; 95% CI, 0.92-1.13) compared with continuers, but discontinuers had higher mortality risk (HR, 1.27; 95% CI, 1.23-1.31).

Conclusions and relevance: In this target trial emulation with CCW in a cohort of LTC residents with AF, AC discontinuation was not associated with higher stroke or bleeding risk. Very high mortality, unmeasured confounding, and reliance on claims-based outcome ascertainment may have limited the ability to better understand the consequences of AC discontinuation on stroke and bleeding.

item.title: JAMA Netw Open: Enteric Fever and Antimicrobial Resistance
item.description:
Importance: Increasing antibiotic resistance in enteric fever (typhoid or paratyphoid fever) is a global public health threat. Knowledge of current antimicrobial resistance patterns and identification of factors associated with acquiring resistant infections can help inform treatment and prevention decisions.

Objective: To estimate the prevalence of antimicrobial-resistant enteric fever in the US after the emergence of extensively drug-resistant Salmonella enterica Typhi in 2016 and describe characteristics of patients with resistant Salmonella Typhi or Paratyphi strains.

Design, setting, and participants: This cross-sectional, laboratory-based study included cases of culture-confirmed enteric fever diagnosed in the US. From January 2016 to December 2020, US health departments submitted epidemiologic data to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) through the National Typhoid and Paratyphoid Fever Surveillance (NTPFS) system, and public health laboratories submitted the corresponding Typhi or Paratyphi isolates to the CDC through the National Antimicrobial Resistance Monitoring System (NARMS). Initial data analysis was complete by March 31, 2023, and the antimicrobial resistance trends analysis was updated in August 2026.

Exposures: Patient variables collected by the NTPFS, including demographic characteristics, travel history, and typhoid vaccination status.

Main outcome and measures: Linked NTPFS-NARMS data from 2016 to 2020 were used to calculate the prevalence of antimicrobial resistance stratified by serotype and to conduct univariable logistic regression to estimate the associations of case characteristics and exposure variables with odds of infection with resistant strains.

Results: In this analysis, 2342 cases were included (1784 typhoid [76.2%], 426 paratyphoid A [18.2%], 114 paratyphoid B [4.9%], and 14 paratyphoid C [0.6%]; 4 isolates [0.2%] had unspecified paratyphoid serotypes). The median patient age was 25 years (IQR, 11-37 years), and patients were male in 1215 of 2325 cases (52.3%). Most patients reported traveling or residing internationally within 30 days of illness onset (1853 of 2217 [81.9%]). From 2016 to 2020, 1635 enteric fever isolates underwent susceptibility testing through NARMS; most Typhi (1061 of 1354 [78.4%]) and Paratyphi A (258 of 274 [94.2%]) isolates were not susceptible to ciprofloxacin. Among 1354 Typhi isolates, resistance exceeded 15% for ampicillin, for chloramphenicol, and for trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole and was 5.5% (74 isolates) for ceftriaxone; 1 Typhi isolate (0.1%) was resistant to azithromycin. Resistance to these agents was not observed among Paratyphi isolates.

Conclusions and relevance: In this cross-sectional study, most typhoid and paratyphoid infections were not susceptible to ciprofloxacin, suggesting that ciprofloxacin should be avoided as empiric therapy for most travel-associated enteric fever cases. Cases of ceftriaxone-resistant typhoid fever were also observed. These findings suggest that treatment of enteric fever should be tailored to susceptibility test results.

item.title: JAMA Netw Open: The Kaiser Permanente Research Bank as a Genomic Data Resource
item.description:
Importance: Large biobanks have become significant engines of discovery-based health research; the collection of large-scale genetic and other molecular data from a deeply phenotyped cohort enables epidemiological studies, biomarker discovery, predictive modeling, and health economic research. In many biobanks, participant data collection is cross-sectional and relies on self-reported medical histories. Furthermore, biobanks may lack ancestral diversity and may need to be enriched for healthy individuals with lower rates of chronic disease.

Objective: To describe the scope and purpose of the Kaiser Permanente Research Bank (KPRB), a large biobank created from medical records, health and socioeconomic surveys, genomic data, and biospecimens of the Kaiser Permanente patient population.

Observations: The KPRB was intended to compile longitudinal medical records data and build a biospecimen collection that included a patient population that was wide and diverse, enabling a wide variety of research pursuits. KPRB participant medical records, survey data, and biospecimens were compiled to enable researcher use. Genomic DNA from participant samples were genotyped and these data were used in genome-wide association studies of blood pressure phenotypes. The KPRB achieved its goal of recruiting and consenting 400 000 participants (449 122 in total) and making available to the broader research community the participant data collected. The KPRB's comprehensive medical records extend retrospectively up to 28 years (median [IQR], 20.9 [14.0-28.7] years) and continue to accumulate patient data for as long as a participant is a KP member. KPRB participants represent a diversity of race and ethnicity groups (38 209 Asian [8.5%], 26 106 Black [5.8%], 50 661 Hispanic [11.3%], 317 630 White [70.7%]) and health outcomes, including both prevalent disease at the time of recruitment and incident disease diagnosed postrecruitment, that are typical of US-based populations. Genomic data collected on nearly all participants has been quality controlled and subjected to imputation. A new genome-wide association study (GWAS) analysis of blood pressure phenotypes in all genotyped KPRB participants has been conducted to validate previously published associations and confirm the quality of both the genomic and medical records data in the KPRB.

Conclusions and relevance: The KPRB, with genetic data generated on a large and diverse cohort with comprehensive medical records, survey data, and biospecimens, will support the growing interest in large biobank-based research and enable new avenues of research. GWAS analyses of common phenotypes measured as part of routine medical care indicated that KPRB is a robust resource linking health outcomes with genetic data that will yield valuable research findings. Access to the KPRB resource is available to external researchers with compelling research proposals through KPRB's Access Review Committee.

item.title: JAMA: Single Intranasal Administration of the Psychedelic Mebufotenin for Treatment-Resistant Depression: A Randomized Clinical Trial
item.description:
Importance: Psychedelics represent a potential breakthrough for treatment-resistant depression; however, the prolonged in-clinic monitoring required for compounds such as psilocybin and lysergic acid diethylamide is a logistical hurdle to widespread use. Intranasal mebufotenin (5-methoxy-N,N-dimethyltryptamine), a 5-hydroxytryptamine 1A (5-HT1A) and 5-HT2A agonist associated with brief psychedelic experiences, may address this limitation.

Objective: To evaluate the safety, efficacy, and time to discharge readiness following a single dose of intranasal mebufotenin benzoate in adults with treatment-resistant depression.

Design, setting, and participants: Phase 2b, randomized, double-blind trial with an 8-week blinded follow-up conducted between September 2023 and April 2025 at 38 sites in Australia, Europe, and the US. Participants were aged 18 to 75 years with moderate to severe major depressive disorder nonresponsive to 2 to 5 antidepressant trials in the current episode. The last date of follow-up was April 28, 2025.

Interventions: After antidepressant washout as needed, participants were randomly assigned to receive a single dose of intranasal mebufotenin benzoate, 8 mg (n = 46), 12 mg (n = 73), or 0.3 mg (a low-dose comparator; n = 74), alongside psychological support.

Main outcomes and measures: The primary end point was total score change on the Montgomery-Åsberg Depression Rating Scale (MADRS; score range, 0-60; higher scores indicate more severe depression) from baseline to day 29 in the 12-mg vs 0.3-mg dose groups. Eighteen secondary end points were assessed for the 12-mg and 8-mg vs 0.3-mg doses. Discharge readiness was assessed starting 90 minutes after dosing.

Results: Among the 193 included participants, the mean age was 41 (SD, 11.1) years and 59.1% were female. From baseline to day 29, treatment with 12-mg intranasal mebufotenin benzoate vs the 0.3-mg dose (the primary end point) was associated with significantly reduced MADRS scores (mean score change, -11.1 [SD, 11.6] vs -5.5 [SD, 9.9], respectively; mean difference, -5.3 [95% CI, -8.9 to -1.8]; P = .003). The 8-mg dose also led to reduced scores from baseline to day 29 (mean score change, -12.5 [SD, 12.7]) vs the 0.3-mg dose (mean difference, -6.2 [95% CI, -10.2 to -2.1]; P = .003). MADRS reductions with the 8-mg and 12-mg doses were similar and significantly greater at all other time points from 2 to 57 days post dose vs the 0.3-mg dose. Day 29 response rates were 35%, 34%, and 12% and remission rates were 26%, 18%, and 8% in the 8-mg, 12-mg, and 0.3-mg dose groups, respectively. Treatment-emergent adverse events were reported in 76%, 85%, and 73% of participants in the 8-mg, 12-mg, and 0.3-mg dose groups, respectively; most events (99.7%) were mild or moderate. Overall, most participants were deemed ready for discharge within 2 hours post dose (85% for 8 mg and 78% for 12 mg).

Conclusions and relevance: In adults with treatment-resistant depression, single doses of intranasal mebufotenin benzoate were well tolerated and produced rapid, robust, and durable reductions in depressive symptoms. Intranasal mebufotenin benzoate may improve treatment access and convenience, requiring a shorter monitoring period and fewer clinic visits compared with psilocybin and esketamine, respectively.

item.category: The New England journal of medicine
item.description:
Background: Patients with extensive-stage small-cell lung cancer have poor outcomes, with a median overall survival of approximately 12 to 13 months. Tarlatamab (a bispecific T-cell engager targeting delta-like ligand 3 [DLL3] and CD3) was previously shown to improve survival as second-line therapy. Whether adding tarlatamab to durvalumab (an anti-programmed death ligand 1 agent) after initial chemoimmunotherapy could significantly improve survival in the context of maintenance therapy after first remission has been unclear.

Methods: In this phase 3, international, open-label, randomized trial, we compared tarlatamab-durvalumab with durvalumab as first-line maintenance therapy in patients with extensive-stage small-cell lung cancer without progression after initial chemoimmunotherapy. Overall survival and progression-free survival were assessed from randomization at the start of maintenance therapy as the primary and key secondary end points, respectively. Results of the prespecified interim analysis (data-cutoff date, July 7, 2026) are reported here.

Results: A total of 563 patients were randomly assigned to receive tarlatamab-durvalumab (282 patients) or durvalumab (281 patients). At a median follow-up of 15.9 months in the tarlatamab-durvalumab group and 16.1 months in the durvalumab group, the estimated median overall survival was 21.1 months (95% confidence interval [CI], 20.8 to could not be estimated) with tarlatamab-durvalumab and 12.7 months (95% CI, 11.2 to 14.8) with durvalumab (hazard ratio for death, 0.42; 95% CI, 0.32 to 0.54; P<0.001). The median progression-free survival was 7.4 months (95% CI, 5.6 to 9.1) with tarlatamab-durvalumab and 1.9 months (95% CI, 1.9 to 2.0) with durvalumab (hazard ratio for disease progression or death, 0.34; 95% CI, 0.28 to 0.42; P<0.001). Adverse events of grade 3 or higher occurred in 46.8% of the patients who received tarlatamab-durvalumab and in 40.6% of those who received durvalumab alone. Cytokine release syndrome, mainly of grade 1 or 2, was seen in nearly half the patients receiving tarlatamab-durvalumab.

Conclusions: Tarlatamab-durvalumab maintenance therapy resulted in significantly longer overall survival and progression-free survival than durvalumab alone among patients with extensive-stage small-cell lung cancer. item.description:
Background: Pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy with a platinum-based agent and pemetrexed is a widely used standard first-line treatment option for patients with programmed death ligand 1 (PD-L1)-negative advanced nonsquamous non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) without targetable genomic alterations, but outcomes remain suboptimal.

Methods: In this phase 3, open-label, randomized trial, we evaluated sacituzumab tirumotecan plus pembrolizumab in patients with previously untreated locally advanced or metastatic nonsquamous NSCLC without targetable genomic alterations and a PD-L1 tumor proportion score of less than 1%. Patients were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive sacituzumab tirumotecan plus pembrolizumab or chemotherapy plus pembrolizumab. The primary end point was progression-free survival as assessed by blinded independent central review. Overall survival was a secondary end point. This report presents the results of the prespecified interim analysis.

Results: A total of 455 patients were randomly assigned to receive sacituzumab tirumotecan plus pembrolizumab (229 patients) or chemotherapy plus pembrolizumab (226 patients). After a median follow-up of 9.7 months, the median progression-free survival was significantly longer with sacituzumab tirumotecan plus pembrolizumab than with chemotherapy plus pembrolizumab (15.0 months vs. 5.7 months; hazard ratio for disease progression or death, 0.49; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.36 to 0.65; P<0.001). An objective response occurred in 50.2% and 47.3% of the patients, respectively, and the median duration of response was 13.6 months and 6.8 months. Overall survival data were immature; the hazard ratio for death was 0.58 (95% CI, 0.38 to 0.88). Adverse events of grade 3 or higher that occurred after the start of treatment were reported in 47.6% of the patients assigned to receive sacituzumab tirumotecan plus pembrolizumab and in 60.6% of those assigned to receive chemotherapy plus pembrolizumab. Stomatitis was common with sacituzumab tirumotecan plus pembrolizumab, but the events were predominantly grade 1 or 2.

Conclusions: Among patients with PD-L1-negative advanced nonsquamous NSCLC without targetable genomic alterations, first-line treatment with sacituzumab tirumotecan plus pembrolizumab led to significantly longer progression-free survival than chemotherapy plus pembrolizumab. Background: Savolitinib is an oral, potent, highly selective MET-tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI). Combination therapy with savolitinib and osimertinib, an epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR)-TKI, has shown activity in patients with EGFR-mutated, advanced non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) with MET overexpression, MET amplification, or both, after progression during EGFR-TKI therapy.

Grade 3 or higher adverse events during treatment were reported in 64% of the patients in the osimertinib-savolitinib group and in 63% of those in the platinum-pemetrexed group.

item.category: The New England journal of medicine
item.description:
Background: The standard of care for patients with muscle-invasive bladder cancer continues to evolve. Whether perioperative durvalumab, with or without tremelimumab, plus neoadjuvant enfortumab vedotin is effective in such patients is unknown.

Methods: In this phase 3 open-label trial, we randomly assigned, in a 1:1:1 ratio, patients with muscle-invasive bladder cancer who were ineligible for or declined cisplatin-based chemotherapy to receive neoadjuvant durvalumab-enfortumab vedotin every 3 weeks for three cycles, followed by radical cystectomy and then adjuvant durvalumab every 4 weeks for nine cycles; neoadjuvant durvalumab-tremelimumab-enfortumab vedotin (tremelimumab for two cycles only), radical cystectomy, and adjuvant durvalumab-tremelimumab (tremelimumab for one cycle only); or radical cystectomy alone (control). The dual primary end points were event-free survival in each of the two durvalumab groups as compared with that in the control group. The two durvalumab groups were not compared with each other. The key secondary end point was overall survival.

Results: In total, 233 patients were assigned to the durvalumab-enfortumab vedotin group, 233 to the durvalumab-tremelimumab-enfortumab vedotin group, and 229 to the control group. Estimated event-free survival at 24 months was 63.5% (95% confidence interval [CI], 56.5 to 69.7) with durvalumab-enfortumab vedotin and 45.1% (95% CI, 38.2 to 51.8) with control (hazard ratio for an event or death, 0.51; 95% CI, 0.38 to 0.67; P<0.001); estimated overall survival at 24 months was 78.4% and 69.4%, respectively (hazard ratio for death, 0.58; 95% CI, 0.40 to 0.83; P = 0.003). Estimated event-free survival at 24 months was 60.1% (95% CI, 53.2 to 66.2) with durvalumab-tremelimumab-enfortumab vedotin (hazard ratio for an event or death vs. control, 0.61; 95% CI, 0.47 to 0.80; P<0.001). item.description:
Background: Divarasib, a next-generation, oral KRAS G12C inhibitor, is more potent and selective in vitro than the first-generation KRAS G12C inhibitors sotorasib and adagrasib.

Methods: In this phase 3, international, open-label trial, patients with previously treated KRAS G12C-mutated advanced or metastatic non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) were randomly assigned to receive divarasib orally at a dose of 400 mg once daily or control treatment (sotorasib orally at a dose of 960 mg once daily or adagrasib orally at a dose of 600 mg twice daily) until the occurrence of disease progression, unacceptable adverse events, loss of clinical benefit, withdrawal of consent, death, or trial termination. item.category: The New England journal of medicine
item.description:
Background: Whether endovascular therapy benefits patients with mild acute ischemic stroke from large-vessel occlusion involving the anterior circulation is uncertain.

Methods: We conducted a multicenter, open-label, randomized trial in China involving patients with acute ischemic stroke of mild clinical severity (defined by a score of <6 on the National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale) that had resulted from large-vessel occlusion involving the anterior circulation. Patients also had neuroimaging features of a small infarct core and a large perfusion-mismatch volume, representing substantial at-risk tissue, within 24 hours after symptom onset or after they were last known to be well. The patients were randomly assigned to undergo endovascular therapy and receive medical management or to receive medical management alone. The primary outcome was an excellent functional outcome (defined by a modified Rankin scale score of 0 [no symptoms] or 1 [no clinically significant disability]) at 90 days.

Results: A total of 304 patients underwent randomization, of whom 300 were included in the modified intention-to-treat population: 144 in the endovascular-therapy group and 156 in the medical-management group. At 90 days, a modified Rankin scale score of 0 or 1 was reported in 69.4% of the patients in the endovascular-therapy group and in 50.0% of those in the medical-management group (odds ratio, 2.32; 95% confidence interval, 1.41 to 3.81; P<0.001). Symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage within 48 hours occurred in 3 patients in each group. Serious procedure-related complications occurred in 19 patients (13.2%) in the endovascular-therapy group. Among all the participants, one death occurred (in the endovascular-therapy group).

Conclusions: In this trial from China involving patients with mild acute ischemic stroke caused by large-vessel occlusion and substantial at-risk tissue on perfusion imaging, endovascular therapy performed within 24 hours after symptom onset plus medical management resulted in better 90-day functional outcomes than medical management alone, without an increase in the risk of symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage but with a high incidence of serious procedural complications. item.description:
Background: Endovascular thrombectomy is an established treatment for acute ischemic stroke. Whether the benefit extends to patients with salvageable brain tissue in the infarct who present more than 24 hours after symptom onset or the time when they were last known to be well is uncertain.

Methods: We conducted an open-label, randomized trial with blinded outcome assessment at comprehensive stroke centers in China. Patients with acute ischemic stroke from large-vessel occlusion of the anterior circulation and imaging-identified salvageable brain tissue at 24 to 72 hours were assigned to receive endovascular therapy plus standard medical care (intervention group) or standard medical care alone (control group). The primary outcome was functional status, defined by the score on the modified Rankin scale (range, 0 to 6, with higher scores indicating greater disability and a score of 6 indicating death) at 90 days, with results assessed as the distribution of scores in each group. Secondary outcomes included disability, neurologic impairment, and safety.

Results: A total of 336 patients were included in the intention-to-treat population, with 168 assigned to each group. The median time from symptom onset or from the point when the patient was last known to be well to randomization was 38.5 hours. Endovascular therapy resulted in a more favorable distribution of modified Rankin scale scores at 90 days than standard medical care alone (common odds ratio for a better functional outcome, 1.74; 95% confidence interval, 1.19 to 2.55). Symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage occurred in 4.8% of the patients in the intervention group and in no patients in the control group, and the 90-day case fatality rate was 6.0% and 1.8%, respectively.

Conclusions: Among patients who presented 24 to 72 hours after an acute ischemic stroke from large-vessel occlusion of the anterior circulation and had imaging-identified salvageable tissue, endovascular therapy resulted in better functional outcomes than standard care but led to a higher risk of intracranial hemorrhage and death. item.title: Crit Care: Consensus recommendations for patient selection and clinical implementation of polymyxin B hemoadsorption in endotoxic septic shock
item.description:
Background: Despite long-standing clinical use and emerging evidence, no structured framework exists guiding clinicians in identifying septic shock patients for endotoxemia assessment, interpretation of the Endotoxin Activity Assay (EAA), or practical implementation of polymyxin B hemoadsorption (PMX-HA) therapy.

Methods: A modified Delphi consensus process was conducted with ten critical care and nephrology experts, compromising a pre-meeting survey, a one-day in-person consensus conference, and iterative voting on draft statements. Consensus was predefined as ≥ 80% agreement.

Results: Consensus was achieved on 20 statements across three domains: (1) operational criteria to prompt endotoxemia assessment in suspected or presumed septic shock, (2) role and interpretation of the EAA, and (3) logistics and clinical implementation of PMX-HA. Key recommendations included standardized criteria to identify eligible patients, EAA thresholds of ≥ 0.60 and < 0.90 to support PMX‑HA consideration, initiation of therapy as early as possible once eligibility is confirmed, with ≤ 36 h from septic shock onset proposed as a pragmatic implementation benchmark, and standardized treatment protocols consisting of two sessions, 24 h apart, targeting 120 min each. A multidisciplinary team model was endorsed for implementation. Identified research priorities were in treatment effect heterogeneity, EAA kinetics, clinical implementation, and healthcare system integration.

Conclusions: These consensus recommendations provide a structured, implementation-focused framework for PMX-HA use in suspected endotoxic shock. The framework emphasizes stepwise operational criteria, biomarker-guided decision-making, multidisciplinary team-based implementation, and standardized protocols. It is intended to support institutions currently using PMX-HA and to assist U.S. clinicians and health systems in preparing for potential adoption pending regulatory approval.

item.title: Lancet: 14-day versus 28-day trifluridine-tipiracil plus bevacizumab for refractory metastatic colorectal cancer (PRABITAS): a pragmatic, multicentre, open-label, randomised, phase 3, non-inferiority trial in Japan
item.description:
Background: Trifluridine-tipiracil (FTD-TPI) plus bevacizumab is the standard treatment for refractory metastatic colorectal cancer. However, the conventional schedule is frequently associated with haematological and gastrointestinal toxicity, which is clinically significant and relevant to patients. A simplified 14-day schedule has been proposed to reduce toxicity, but whether this treatment preserves survival has not been established in a randomised trial. We therefore aimed to assess whether the 14-day schedule is non-inferior to the conventional schedule for overall survival.

Methods: PRABITAS was a pragmatic, multicentre, open-label, randomised, phase 3, non-inferiority trial conducted in 178 hospitals in Japan. Patients with refractory metastatic colorectal cancer were randomly assigned (1:1) using a minimisation algorithm, stratified by Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status, RAS mutational status, and institution, to FTD-TPI (35 mg/m2 orally twice daily) plus bevacizumab (5 mg/kg intravenously) on either a conventional 28-day (FTD-TPI on days 1-5 and 8-12; bevacizumab on days 1 and 15) or 14-day schedule (FTD-TPI on days 1-5; bevacizumab on day 1). Eligibility criteria were broadened compared with those of conventional explanatory trials, and trial procedures were aligned with routine clinical practice. The primary endpoint was overall survival, analysed in the intention-to-treat population, with a prespecified non-inferiority margin of 1·25. Safety was assessed in all patients who received at least one dose. Missing data were not imputed. This trial is registered with the Japan Registry of Clinical Trials, jRCTs041230120, and is closed to enrolment.

Findings: Between Dec 26, 2023, and May 20, 2025, we randomly assigned 972 patients, of whom 970 (99%) constituted the intention-to-treat population after two were excluded because they were randomly assigned before site approval (486 [50%] to the 28-day treatment group, 292 [60%] men and 194 [40%] women]; and 484 [50%] to the 14-day treatment group, 264 [55%] men and 220 [45%] women). Median follow-up was 17·9 months (IQR 14·3-22·6). Median overall survival was 10·3 months (95% CI 9·5-11·6) in the 28-day group and 11·3 months (10·2-12·5) in the 14-day group (stratified hazard ratio 0·93 [95% CI 0·80-1·08]). The 12-month overall survival rates were 44·0% (95% CI 39·5-48·5) in the 28-day group and 47·5% (42·9-52·0) in the 14-day group. Neutropenia grade 3 or worse was reduced in the 14-day group (13% vs 39%; absolute difference 25 percentage points [95% CI 20-31]), as was anorexia grade 2 or worse (15% vs 26%; absolute difference 11 percentage points [6-16]). Two treatment-related deaths occurred in the 14-day group and none in the 28-day group.

Interpretation: A 14-day schedule of FTD-TPI plus bevacizumab was non-inferior to the conventional 28-day schedule for overall survival, while reducing haematological and gastrointestinal toxicity. These findings support this simplified schedule as the new standard for FTD-TPI plus bevacizumab in refractory metastatic colorectal cancer.

item.title: Am J Emerg Med: Implementation of regional interfacility transfer guidelines for patients with isolated facial trauma: A preliminary report
item.category: The American journal of emergency medicine
item.description:
Objective: Secondary overtriage (SO) of isolated craniomaxillofacial (CMF) fractures overwhelm trauma centers and represent a significant resource burden while ultimately delaying patient care. The objective of this study was to implement an interfacility transfer protocol at a tertiary level 1 trauma center and review the preliminary utilization findings.

Methods: A tertiary academic medical center adopted the protocol via the AgileMD pathway in regional referral centers. The protocol indicates the necessity of on-call specialist consultation based on a patient's clinical presentation. This study conducted a retrospective cohort analysis for patients with isolated CMF trauma and AgileMD pathway activation over a one year period. The main outcome was transfer center activation.

Results: The pathway was utilized 55 times for isolated CMF trauma patients in one year. The majority of traumas involved nasal bone fractures (52.7%) and were most often caused by falls (49.1%). On-call specialist consultation occurred 18.2% of the time - down from 100% of cases prior to guideline institution. The majority of patients (78.2%) were discharged with 40.9% follow-up, while 16.4% were transferred. These dispositions followed the guidelines 90.9% of the time.

Conclusions: This is the first pilot study on the implementation of isolated CMF trauma interfacility transfer guidelines. The 81.8% reduction in on-call specialist consultation suggests a meaningful call burden reduction for surgical providers, while a discharge rate of 78.2% and outpatient follow-up rate consistent with pre-implementation levels reflects significant preservation of trauma resources. Broader adoption of similar protocols can further reduce SO, hospital costs, and wait times.

item.description:
Importance: In randomized clinical trials, sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitor use was associated with increased hemoglobin and hematocrit compared with placebo. However, the magnitude and importance of this association remain unclear.

Objective: To evaluate the associations between SGLT2 inhibitor use and levels of hemoglobin, hematocrit, and markers of iron metabolism and erythropoiesis compared with placebo or active comparator.

Data sources: PubMed, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL) were searched from inception to July 22, 2026.

Study selection: Randomized, double-masked clinical trials comparing SGLT2 inhibitor use with placebo or active comparators in patients with 1 or more of the following conditions: cardiovascular disease, diabetes, heart failure, and chronic kidney disease.

Data extraction and synthesis: Three reviewers independently extracted data and results were pooled using random-effects meta-analysis.

Main outcomes and measures: Primary outcomes were changes in hemoglobin and hematocrit. Secondary outcomes were changes in red blood cell concentration, erythropoietin (EPO), and iron measures (serum iron, ferritin, transferrin saturation, and hepcidin).

Results: A total of 85 randomized clinical trials were analyzed (median [IQR] duration, 24 [12-32] weeks), including 70 543 participants (mean [SD] age, 62.4 [9.4] years; 25 334 female [35.9%]). Mean (SD) baseline hemoglobin was 13.6 (1.5) g/dL; baseline hematocrit was 41.5% (4.9). Seventy-eight clinical trials (67 208 participants) compared SGLT2 inhibitors with placebo, and 7 clinical trials (3335 participants) used active comparators, most commonly sitagliptin (2 trials [1158 participants]). From baseline to follow-up, hemoglobin changed by 0.55 g/dL (95% CI, 0.49 to 0.61 g/dL; P < .001) in the SGLT2 inhibitor group, and -0.08 g/dL (95% CI, -0.13 to -0.03 g/dL; P = .003) in the control group (difference, 0.60 g/dL; 95% CI, 0.55 to 0.66 g/dL; P < .001). From baseline to follow-up, hematocrit changed by 2.17% (95% CI, 1.95% to 2.39%; P < .001) in the SGLT2 inhibitor group and -0.13% (95% CI, -0.28% to 0.01%; P = .07) in the control group (difference, 2.36%; 95% CI, 2.19% to 2.52%; P < .001). Of the 6 secondary outcomes, 4 showed significant associations with SGLT2 inhibitors, including increased EPO (2.35 mIU/mL in SGLT2 inhibitor group vs 0.04 mIU/mL in control group; difference, 2.11 mIU/mL [95% CI, 0.5-3.71 mIU/mL]; P = .01) and decreased transferrin saturation (-2.2% in SGLT2 inhibitor group vs -0.10% in control group; difference, -0.84% [95% CI, -1.21% to -0.47%]; P < .001).

Conclusions and relevance: In a meta-analysis of randomized clinical trials, compared with control, SGLT2 inhibitor use was associated with small statistically significant increases in hemoglobin and hematocrit levels. The clinical significance of these findings is unclear.

item.title: JAMA Netw Open: Maternal Vaccination vs Nirsevimab Use and Respiratory Syncytial Virus Infection Among Full-Term Infants
item.description:
Importance: Since 2023, infants can be protected from respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) through a vaccine (RSVpreF) for pregnant persons or a monoclonal antibody (nirsevimab) for infants.

Objective: To assess the relative product effectiveness (rPE) of maternal RSVpreF vs infant nirsevimab against RSV infection and hospitalization among infants born in the 2023 to 2025 RSV seasons.

Design, setting, and participants: This retrospective cohort study included full-term infants born at Kaiser Permanente Northern California (KPNC), an integrated health care system with approximately 40 000 births each year, from December 3, 2023, to March 30, 2024, or September 29, 2024, to March 15, 2025. Infants protected by RSVpreF were matched to infants protected with nirsevimab with optimal full matching (up to 1:5), adjusting for birth week, sex, and maternal factors. Each group was also compared with infants with no protection, matching unprotected infants to both RSVpreF and nirsevimab infants (up to 1:10).

Exposures: Maternal RSVpreF at 32 to 36 weeks' gestation or infant nirsevimab through age 7 days.

Main outcomes and measures: Polymerase chain reaction (PCR)-confirmed RSV and RSV hospitalization (PCR-confirmed RSV 10 days before to 7 days after hospitalization) in infants aged 8 to 180 days or through RSV season end (April 30 in both seasons). rPE was estimated from age 8 to 180 days using restricted mean time lost.

Results: Of 15 124 matched infants (7729 [51.1%] male) in the primary analysis, 146 (0.97%) had RSV infection (106 of 11 293 [0.94%] in RSVpreF group and 40 of 3831 [1.04%] in nirsevimab group) and 12 (0.08%) were hospitalized (7 [0.06%] in RSVpreF group and 5 [0.13%] in nirsevimab group). The rPE of RSVpreF vs nirsevimab was -5.3% (95% CI, -44.8% to 23.4%) against infection and 61.5% (95% CI, -10.8% to 86.7%) against hospitalization. Compared with no protection, RSVpreF rPE was 69.3% (95% CI, 59.9% to 76.6%) against infection and 86.4% (95% CI, 66.4% to 94.5%) against hospitalization; nirsevimab rPE was 65.2% (95% CI, 51.0%-75.4%) and 73.8% (95% CI, 33.4%-89.7%), respectively.

Conclusion: In this cohort study of infants born in the 2023 to 2024 and 2024 to 2025 RSV seasons, no statistically significant difference between maternal RSVpreF and infant nirsevimab in RSV infection or hospitalization was detected. Compared with no protection, both products were associated with fewer infections and hospitalizations. This study supports current US guidelines for either maternal RSVpreF or infant nirsevimab to protect all infants from RSV.

item.title: Crit Care Med: Role of Mitochondrial Impairment in Sepsis-Induced Platelet Activation
item.description:
Objectives: Sepsis-induced mitochondrial impairment has been described in different organs, in both animal models and humans. Excessive radical oxygen species (ROS) could be involved in this phenomenon. As a result, antioxidants have been proposed as a potential therapeutic strategy, although results remain controversial. Platelet hyperactivation is considered a central pathogenic mechanism in the development of sepsis-induced organ damage. In this study, we aimed to determine whether mitochondrial dysfunction contributes to platelet hyperactivation during sepsis. We also evaluated the effect of ROS scavenging using the mitochondria-targeted antioxidant MitoTEMPO.

Design: Laboratory investigation.

Setting: University Hospital.

Patients and subjects: Patients with sepsis/septic shock (n = 3/7), nonseptic burn patients (n = 10), and healthy control subjects (n = 10).

Interventions: Platelet mitochondria and isolated platelets from healthy donors were treated in vitro with plasma from patients with sepsis/septic shock and healthy subjects, before and after preincubation with MitoTEMPO.

Measurements and main results: We measured platelet oxygen consumption rates in isolated human platelets using the Seahorse Extracellular Flux Analyzer. Platelet mitochondrial respiratory chain enzyme activity was measured in mitochondria-enriched fractions by spectrophotometry. Platelet aggregation in platelet-rich plasma was analyzed using light-transmission aggregometry, and leukocyte-platelet adhesion in whole blood by flow cytometry.We found that incubating platelets with septic plasma significantly reduced basal, maximal, and adenosine triphosphate-linked oxygen consumption rate. Incubation of platelet mitochondria with septic plasma also reduced platelet Complex I activity, compared with healthy plasma or plasma from nonseptic burn patients. This decrease was associated with an increase in Epinephrine-induced platelet activation. Preincubating platelets with the mitochondria-selective ROS scavenger MitoTEMPO significantly reversed these effects.

Conclusions: Our results show that the mitochondria-selective ROS scavenger MitoTEMPO prevents mitochondrial dysfunction and enhances platelet activation induced by septic plasma in human platelets in vitro. This may help in designing new therapeutic approaches to prevent sepsis-induced organ damage mediated by mitochondrial dysfunction and platelet hyperactivation.

Objective: To compare trastuzumab rezetecan vs physician's choice of chemotherapy in patients with ERBB2-low metastatic breast cancer.

Eligible patients were females aged 18 to 75 years with centrally confirmed ERBB2-low (immunohistochemistry [IHC] 1+ or IHC 2+/in-situ hybridization [ISH]-negative) unresectable locally recurrent or metastatic breast cancer who had received 1 or fewer prior lines of chemotherapy for metastatic disease, with prior endocrine therapy required for hormone receptor-positive disease. Interventions: Patients were randomly assigned (1:1) to receive trastuzumab rezetecan (6.4 mg/kg intravenously every 3 weeks; n = 277) or physician's choice of chemotherapy (n = 274).

Main outcomes and measures: The primary end point was progression-free survival assessed by blinded independent central review in chemotherapy-naive patients and the overall population.

Conclusions and relevance: Trastuzumab rezetecan provided significant progression-free survival benefit over physician's choice of chemotherapy in patients with ERBB2-low advanced breast cancer, with benefit observed across all key subgroups. It exhibited the potential as a new treatment option with a distinct safety profile in this setting.

item.title: J Am Coll Emerg Physicians Open: Assessment of Carotid Doppler Parameters to Evaluate Volume Status: A Prospective Observational Study
item.category: Journal of the American College of Emergency Physicians open
item.description:
Objectives: Accurate assessment of volume status and fluid responsiveness is essential to guide fluid therapy, as unnecessary fluid administration may lead to fluid overload and adverse outcomes. Carotid Doppler ultrasound has emerged as a rapid, noninvasive alternative to more technically demanding echocardiographic measures. This study evaluated the utility of carotid Doppler-derived corrected flow time (FTc) and velocity-time integral (VTI), and their changes after passive leg raise (PLR), in assessing volume status and preload responsiveness.

Methods: We conducted a prospective observational study during Ramadan at a tertiary academic medical center. A total of 202 participants were enrolled, including 103 fasting individuals assessed during presumed relative dehydration and after rehydration, and 99 nonfasting hydrated controls. Carotid Doppler measurements of FTc, VTI, and Vmax were obtained before and after PLR. Diagnostic performance of percent changes in FTc (ΔFTc) and VTI (ΔVTI) was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic analysis.

Results: Participants in the fasting group underwent a mean fasting duration of 12.4 ± 1.1 hours and consumed a mean of 920 ± 352 mL of fluid after breaking the fast. PLR induced significantly greater increases in FTc and VTI during presumed relative dehydration. A ≥10% increase in VTI was observed in 57.2% of presumed relative dehydrated participants compared with 26.3% of hydrated controls and 20.4% of rehydrated participants. Similarly, a ≥5% increase in FTc was observed in 47.6%, 17.2%, and 22.3% of participants, respectively. Receiver operating characteristic analysis demonstrated moderate discriminatory performance for presumed relative dehydration, with areas under the curve of 0.708 for ΔVTI and 0.715 for ΔFTc. Optimal cutoff values were 5.92% for ΔVTI and 5.05% for ΔFTc.

Conclusion: Carotid Doppler-derived FTc and VTI are promising noninvasive markers of volume status and preload responsiveness. ΔVTI demonstrated greater sensitivity, whereas ΔFTc provided higher specificity, supporting the potential role of carotid Doppler ultrasound as a practical bedside tool for hemodynamic assessment.
